translation.quality: The source edition describes its English as machine-assisted and post-edited and cautions that errors may remain. These passages were extracted from the al-Tabari-labeled sections; they have not been independently checked against the Arabic.

x: We have already explained the meaning of His statement, Alif, Lam, Ra, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. As for his saying:
h
A Book which We have revealed to you
, its meaning is: This is
h
a Book which We have revealed to you

, O Muhammad, meaning the Qur’an, that you may bring mankind out of darkness into the light, meaning: to guide them with it from the darkness of misguidance and disbelief, to the light and radiance of faith, and to show the people of ignorance and blindness the paths of guidance and right direction. His saying:
h
By the permission of their Lord

, meaning by their Lord’s success in this and His kindness to them, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, meaning: to the straight path of God, which is His religion that He has chosen and legislated for His creation. Al-Hamid is a verbal noun, inflected from mafool to fa'il, and its meaning is: the one who is praised for his deeds.

And the Most High attributed the bringing of people out of darkness into the light by their Lord’s permission for them to do so, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is the guide of His creation and the one who grants success to those He loves among them to faith, since it was from him that He called them to it and informed them of what they have in it and what they are responsible for. Thus He demonstrated the correctness of the statement of the people of affirmation who attributed the actions of the servants to themselves as an acquisition, and to God, may His praise be exalted, as creation and management, and the corruption of the statement of the people of predestination who denied that God has any role in that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
To bring people out of darkness into the light
, meaning from misguidance to guidance.

x: The reading of that differed. The general reading of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham is: God, to whom belongs what is in the heavens, raising the name God as the subject, and making his statement: to whom belongs what is in the heavens its predicate. The people of Iraq, Kufa and Basra generally read it as: God who, with the name God in the genitive case, following that of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, and both are in the genitive case. The Arab scholars differed in their interpretation of it, as it was read in this way. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Alaa that he used to read it in the accusative case. He said: Its meaning is: By the permission of their Lord to the path of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens. He said: It is from the word mukhtar which means to bring forward, and he gives an example of it with the saying of the speaker: I passed by the elegant Abdullah.

The speech that is placed in place of the noun is the adjective, then the noun is placed in place of the adjective, so its parsing follows the parsing of the adjective that was placed in place of the noun, as some poets said: If you were noble and brave, you would not fear the attacks of the evil wolf. As for Al-Kisa’i, he used to say, as was mentioned about him: Whoever lowers it, he wants to make it one word, and he follows the lowering with the lowering, and he used to recite with the lowering.

The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, and each one of them has been recited by imams of the reciters. Their meaning is the same, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. It may be possible that the one who read it in the nominative case intended the meaning of the genitive case in the following of the words one after the other, but it was in the nominative case because it was separated from the verse before it, as God Almighty said: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties to the end of the verse, then He said: The repentant, the worshippers. The meaning of his saying:
h
To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth

, is God who owns everything in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He says to his prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have sent down to you this book so that you may call My servants to worship one who has this description, and calls to worship one who has no power to harm or benefit them or himself from the gods and idols.

Then He, may His praise be glorified, threatened those who disbelieved in Him and did not respond to the call of His Messenger to what he called them to of sincere monotheism for Him, saying: And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment, meaning: the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell, for those who denied His oneness and worshipped other than Him, the severe punishment of God.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of that differed.

The general reading of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham is: God, to whom belongs what is in the heavens, raising the name God as the subject, and making his statement: to whom belongs what is in the heavens its predicate.
The people of Iraq, Kufa and Basra generally read it as: God who, with the name God in the genitive case, following that of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, and both are in the genitive case.
The Arab scholars differed in their interpretation of it, as it was read in this way.
It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Alaa that he used to read it in the accusative case.
As for Al-Kisa’i, he used to say, as was mentioned about him: Whoever lowers it, he wants to make it one word, and he follows the lowering with the lowering, and he used to recite with the lowering.
Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, and each one of them has been recited by imams of the reciters.

It may be possible that the one who read it in the nominative case intended the meaning of the genitive case in the following of the words one after the other, but it was in the nominative case because it was separated from the verse before it, as God Almighty said: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties to the end of the verse, then He said: The repentant, the worshippers.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His statement:
h
Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter

, is those who choose the life of this world and its pleasures and the sins of God in it, over obeying God and the beneficial deeds that will bring them closer to His pleasure in the Hereafter: And they hinder from the way of God, meaning: And they prevent whoever wants to believe in God and follow His Messenger according to what he brought from God, from believing in him and following him, and they seek to make it crooked, meaning: And they seek the way of God, which is His religion with which He sent His Messenger, crooked, distorting and changing it with lies and falsehood. And crookedness, with a kasra on the ‘ayn and a fatha on the ‘waw, in religion, land, and everything that is not upright. As for everything that is upright, such as a wall, spear, or tooth, then it is said with a fatha on the ‘ayn and the ‘waw, both of them are crooked.

God Almighty says: Those are in far error, meaning those unbelievers who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter. He says: They are far astray from the truth, taking it without guidance, and deviating from the right path. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of ala in his saying: ala al-akhira.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: Connect the verb with ala as it was said: They struck him with the sword, meaning with the sword. This is because all of these letters are connected with it and deleted, like the Arabs’ saying: I descended upon Zayd, and I passed by Zayd, meaning: I passed by him, and I descended upon him.
Some of them said: This was only included because the verb conveys its meaning from the verbs. In his saying:
h
They prefer the life of this world
, its meaning is that
h
they prefer the life of this world
over the afterlife, and for this reason it was included. I have explained this and similar things in more than one place in the book, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

God Almighty says: And We did not send to any nation, O Muhammad, before you and before your people, a messenger except with the language and tongue of the nation to which We sent him, to make clear to them, meaning: to make them understand what God sent him with to them of His commands and prohibitions, to establish God’s proof against them. Then success and failure are in the hand of God, so He causes whomever He wills to fail to accept what His Messenger brought to him from Him, and He grants success to accept it whomever He wills. This is a nominative and leads astray, because it is intended to begin with it and not to connect with what came before it, as it was said: That We may make clear to you and establish in the wombs whomever We will, And He is the Exalted in Might, who does not refrain from what He wills of misguidance or guidance for whomever He wills that for him, the Wise, in His granting of success to faith for whomever He guides to it, and in His misguidance for whomever He guides to it, and in His misguidance for whomever He misguides from it, and in other than that of His management.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people

, meaning the language of his people, whatever it was. God Almighty said: To make clear to them, that is, to whom he was sent, to take that as an argument. God Almighty said: “Then God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”

x: God Almighty says: And We sent Moses with Our proofs and arguments before you, O Muhammad, just as We sent you to your people with similar proofs and arguments, such as:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hasan Al-Ashib told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Abu Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And We sent Moses with Our signs
, he said: with clear proofs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We sent Moses with Our signs
, he said: the nine signs, the flood and what was with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We sent Moses with Our signs, he said: the nine clear signs.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And His saying:
h
That you bring your people out of darkness into the light
, just as We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, this Book so that you may bring people out of darkness into the light by the permission of their Lord. And what He means by His saying:
h
That you bring your people out of darkness into the light
, is that you call them from misguidance to guidance, and from disbelief to faith, just as:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We sent Moses with Our signs
, saying, ‘Bring your people out of darkness into the light,’ meaning: from misguidance to guidance.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. And His statement:
h
And remind them of the days of God

, God Almighty says: He admonished them of the blessings He bestowed upon them in the days that passed, so He was satisfied with mentioning the days from mentioning the blessings that He meant, because they were days that were known to them, in which God bestowed great blessings upon them, in which He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, after they were in humiliating torment, and He drowned their enemy Pharaoh and his people, and He gave them their land, their homes, and their wealth. Some Arab scholars said: Its meaning is: To frighten them with the punishment that befell the people of Aad, Thamud, and others like them, and to pardon the others. He said: It is in meaning like your saying: Take them with severity and gentleness.

x: Others of them said: We have found evidence for naming blessings as days in their speech. Then he cited as evidence for that the words of Amr ibn Kulthum: And days were long for us, in which we disobeyed the King and refused to obey Him. He said: It may be that He made it a long and glorious day because of their blessings upon the people during it. He said: This is evidence for those who said:
h
And remind them of the days of God

, of the blessings of God? Then he said: It may be that it was called a long and glorious day because of their superiority over the kingdom and their protection from it, so their days are a long and glorious day for their enemies.

The one who said this statement, that this verse contains evidence that the meaning of days is blessings, has no basis. Because ʿAmr ibn Kulthum only described the days that he described as being radiant, due to the honor of his clan there and their refusal to submit to the king in obedience. This is like the people saying: So-and-so did not have a white day, meaning that he did not have a day mentioned for good. As for his describing it as long, it is not described as long except in a state of hardship, as Al-Nabigha said: I am tired of them, O Umaima, and I am suffering a night in which the stars are slow Amr described it as long because it was very unpleasant for the enemies of his people. There is no reason for that other than what I said. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Laith,
m: on the Surat Ibrahim 14:5 And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring your people out of darkness into the light
h
and remind them of the days of God
. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful." authority of Mujahid:
h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: of the blessings of God.

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: of the blessings of God.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abthar told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: By the days of God, he said: By the blessings of God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: of the blessings that He bestowed upon them, He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and split the sea for them, and shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Habib bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: of the blessings of God.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: He reminded them of God’s blessings upon them.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: of the blessings of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And remind them of the days of God

, he said: His days in which He took revenge on the people of His disobedience from the nations, frightening them with them and warning them against them, and reminding them that what happened to those before them would happen to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abu, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And remind them of the days of God
, he said: God’s blessings.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Ubayd God or someone else, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And remind them of the days of God

, he said: of the blessings of God. Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person, meaning: Indeed in the days that preceded My blessings upon them, meaning upon the people of Moses, are signs, meaning lessons and admonitions, for every patient and grateful person, meaning: for everyone who is patient in obeying God and is grateful to Him for the blessings He bestowed upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. He said: What a good servant is the servant who, when tested, is patient, and when given something, is grateful.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, when Moses, son of Imran, said to his people from the Children of Israel: Remember the favor of God upon you, which He bestowed upon you, when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, meaning: when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh’s religion and obedience, who subjected you to the worst torment, meaning they made you taste severe torment, and slaughtered your sons, while making you taste severe torment, they slaughtered your sons. The waw was inserted in this place because what was meant by his saying: and they slaughter your sons, is the report that the people of Pharaoh were torturing the Children of Israel with types of torture other than slaughtering and with slaughtering. As for another place in the Qur’an, it came without the waw: (They subject you to the worst torture, they slaughter your sons), in one place, and in another place they kill your sons, and the waw was not inserted in the places where it was not inserted because what was meant by his saying: they slaughter, and by his saying: they kill, is to clarify the characteristics of the torture that they subjected them to.

And the same is the case with every sentence that is intended to be detailed, so the waw is used to detail it, and if it is intended to be connected to it with something other than it and other than its detail, then the waw is used.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when Moses said to his people
, ‘Remember the favor of God upon you,’ God’s favors upon you and His days. And his saying:
h
And they spare your women
, he says:
h
And they spare your women

and leave killing them, and that is their sparing of them, and we have explained that in what is sufficient, so there is no need to repeat it in this place, and its meaning is: They leave them and life, and from it is the report that was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Kill the elders of the polytheists and spare their young, meaning keep them alive and do not kill them. And in that is a great trial for you from your Lord, God Almighty says: In what the people of Pharaoh do to you of various types of punishment, is a great trial for you from your Lord, meaning a trial and test for you, from your Lord, which is great. And the trial, in this context, may be a blessing, or it may be from the trials that befall people of hardships.

x: God Almighty says: And remember also when your Lord gave you permission. And ta'han is derived from adhan. The Arabs may have put ta'han in place of af'al, as they said: Aw'adhu and A'dhan, meaning the same thing.

i: And adhan means to know, as Al-Harith bin Halza said:
x: She let us know the names of a Lord who is eternally present and never tires of remaining.
He means by his saying: you informed us, you informed us.

c: It was reported on the authority of Ibn Masʿu,
m: may God be pleased with him, that he used to recite: And when your Lord declared: And when your Lord said.

c: Al-Harith told me that, he said, Abdul Aziz told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash,
m: on his authority.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when your Lord gave permission
, and when your Lord said, that is: the permission. And His saying:
h
If you are grateful
, I will surely increase you, means:
h
If you are grateful

to your Lord, by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, I will surely increase His favors upon you and His blessings upon you, in addition to what He has given you of salvation from the people of Pharaoh and deliverance from their punishment. And another statement was made about this, which is:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us,
m: I heard Ali bin Saleh say about the words of God Almighty:
h
If you are grateful
, I will surely increase you, he said: meaning of My obedience.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said,
m: I heard Ali bin Saleh, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us:
m: h
If you are grateful
, I will surely increase you, he said: of My obedience.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Malik bin Mughol told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you are grateful
, I will surely increase you, he said: of My obedience.

x: There is no basis for this statement to be understood, because there is no mention of obedience in this place, so it is said: If you thank me for it, I will give you more of it. Rather, the mention of the report of God’s favor upon the people of Moses was made in His saying: And when Moses said to his people, ‘Remember the favor of God upon you,’ then he informed them that God informed them that if they thanked Him for this favor, He would give them more of it. So what is required in the concept is that the meaning of the statement is: He gave them more of His favors, not of what was not mentioned of obedience, unless what is meant by it is:
h
If you are grateful

and obey me with gratitude, I will give you more of the reasons for gratitude that will help you with it, so that would be a basis. And His statement: And if you disbelieve, then indeed, My punishment is severe, meaning: If you, O people, disbelieve in God’s blessing and deny it by not thanking Him for it, disobeying His commands and prohibitions, and committing sins against Him, then indeed, My punishment is severe, I will punish you as I punish those of My creation who disbelieve in Me.
Some of the Basrans used to say about the meaning of his saying:
h
And when your Lord gave permission
, and your Lord gave permission: and he said: When is one of the extra letters. And we have shown the corruption of that previously.

God Almighty says: And Moses said to his al-Nas 114:If you disbelieve, O people, and deny the favor of God which He has bestowed upon you, you, and everyone on earth does the same as you did, then God is Free of need, of you and of them from all of His creation, He has no need of your thanking Him for His favors from all of you, Praiseworthy, Possessor of praise to His creation for what He has bestowed upon them, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali:
m: Then God is Rich, he said: Rich from His creation, Praiseworthy, he said: Praised by them.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Moses said to his al-Nas 114:O my al-Nas 114:Has there not come to you the report of those before you? He says: The report of those before you from the nations that passed before you, the people of Noah, ʿAd, and Thamud.

The people of Noah are explained by them from those who, and ʿAd is connected to the people of Noah, “and those after them,” meaning after the people of Noah, ʿAd, and Thamud, none knows them except God, He says: None can count their number and none knows their number except God, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun:
m: And ‘Ad and Thamud and those after them, none knows them except God, he said: The genealogists lied.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maimun, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, who said, Ibn Masoud told us that
m: he used to recite it, And ‘Ad and Thamud and those after them, none knows them except God, then he would say: The genealogists lied.

c: Ibn al-Muntha told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Isa ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. His statement:
h
Their messengers came to them with clear proofs

, means: These nations were visited by their messengers whom God sent to call them to sincere worship of Him, with clear proofs, meaning with arguments and evidence of the truth of what they called them to, miracles. And his saying:
h
They put their hands in their mouths
, the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: They bit their fingers, out of anger at them for calling them to what they called them to.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
They put their hands in their mouths
, he said: They bit them in anger.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So they put their hands over their mouths
, he said in anger, like this, and he bit his hand.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
They put their hands in their mouths
, he said: They bit it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hammani told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
They put their hands in their mouths
, he said: They bit the tips of their fingers.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of ʿAbdullah, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And they put their hands in their mouths
, he said: that he put his finger in his mouth.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abu Qatan told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: So
h
they put their hands in their mouths
, and Shu’bah placed the tips of his left fingers on his mouth.

c: Al-Hasan told us, Yahya bin Abbad told us, Shu’bah told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hubayrah, who said, Abdullah said:
m: h
They put their hands in their mouths
, he said like this, and he put his fingers in his mouth.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Shu’bah told us,
m: Abu Ishaq said, he informed us on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse:
h
And they put their hands in their mouths

. Abu Ali said: And Affan showed us, and he put the tips of his fingers extended in his Surat Ibrahim 14:9 Has there not come to you the news of those before you - the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them except God.
h
Their messengers came to them with clear proofs

, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, "Indeed, we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us." mouth, and he mentioned that Shu’bah showed him like that.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan and Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
They put their hands in their mouths
, he said: They bit their fingertips. Sufyan said: They bit out of anger.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they put their hands in their mouths
, and he recited: They bit their fingertips in anger, he said: This is,
h
they put their hands in their mouths
. He said: They put their fingers
h
in their mouths
. And he said: When a person becomes angry, he bites his hand.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that when they heard the Book of God, they were amazed by it and put their hands over their mouths.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they put their hands to their mouths, he said: When they heard the Book of God, they were amazed, and they put their hands back to their mouths.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they denied them with their mouths.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
So they put their hands over their mouths
, he said: They rejected their statement and denied them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their messengers came to them with clear proofs
, but they put their hands to their mouths, meaning: Their people denied their messengers and rejected what they had brought of clear proofs, and they rejected them with their mouths,
h
and they said
: We are in doubt about what you are calling us to, disturbing.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They put their hands over their mouths
, he said: They returned to the messengers what they had brought.

x: It seems that Mujahid interpreted his statement,
h
They put their hands in their mouths
, to mean: They returned the hands of God, which if they had accepted them would have been hands and blessings to them, but they did not accept them. And he interpreted his statement,
h
In their mouths
, to mean: With their mouths, meaning: With their tongues that are
h
in their mouths

. It was mentioned that some Arabs heard: May God admit you into Paradise, meaning: into Paradise, and this verse is recited. I would rather have her than Laqit and his gang, but I do not want her to have Sinbas. He wants: I want her, meaning his daughter, over a foundling, and I do not want her over my tribe.
Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they were placing their hands over the mouths of the messengers, in response to their words and to deny them.

Others said: This is a parable, but what is meant is that they refrained from saying the truth that they were commanded to say, and they did not believe in it or submit. He said: It is said to a man if he refrains from answering and does not respond: He put his hand in his mouth.
Some of them mentioned that the Arabs say: I spoke to so-and-so about a need and he put his hand in his mouth, if he was silent about it and did not respond.
This is also a statement that has no basis, because God Almighty has informed us about them that they said: We have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, so they responded with denial.
The most correct of these sayings in my opinion in interpreting this verse is the saying we mentioned on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud: that they put their hands back
h
in their mouths

and bit them out of rage at the Messengers, just as God Almighty described their brothers among the hypocrites when He said: And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. This is the well-known statement and the understood meaning of putting the hand back in the mouth. And His statement:
h
And they said
, ‘Indeed, we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent,’ means that the Almighty says:
h
And they said

to their messengers: Indeed, we have disbelieved in that with which He Who sent you sent you, of calling us to abandon the worship of idols and statues, ‘and indeed, we are in doubt,’ about the truth of what you are calling us to of the oneness of God, disturbing, meaning that this doubt makes us doubt, that is, it causes us to be suspicious and accused of it.
It is said: A man is suspicious, if he brings something suspicious, he raises suspicion.

evidence.text: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, who said, Ibn Masoud told us that he used to recite it, And ‘Ad and Thamud and those after them, none knows them except God, then he would say: The genealogists lied.
It was mentioned that some Arabs heard: May God admit you into Paradise, meaning: into Paradise, and this verse is recited.

x: God Almighty says: The messengers of the nations to whom their messengers came said: Is there any doubt in God, that He is the One who deserves divinity and worship over you, O people, without all of His creation? “And His statement: ‘Creator of the heavens and the earth,’ means: Creator of the heavens and the earth. ‘He calls you to forgive you some of your sins,’ means: He calls you to His Oneness and obedience. ‘To forgive you some of your sins,’ means: He covers up some of your sins by pardoning them, so He does not punish you for them. ‘And delay you,’ means: He postpones your appointed times, so He does not punish you in the immediate future and destroy you, but He delays you until the time that is written in the Mother of the Book that He will take you, and it is the appointed time that He has named for you. The nations said to them: “You are only human beings like us,” in form and appearance, and you are not angels. What you want with what you say to us is to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. He says: You only want with your saying to turn us away from the worship of what our fathers used to worship of idols. Then bring us a clear authority, he says: Then bring us an argument for what you say, that will show us its truth and correctness, so that we will know that you are right in what you say.

God Almighty says: They said to the nations to whom the messengers came: We are only human beings like you. You are right in what you say. You are only human beings like us. We are only human beings from the children of Adam, human beings like you. But God bestows His favor upon whomever He wills of His servants. He says: But God bestows favor upon whomever He wills of His creation, guiding him and granting him success to the truth. It was not for us to come to you with an argument and proof for what we call you to, except by God’s permission. He says: Except by God’s command to us to do so. And in God let the believers put their trust. He says: And in God let whoever believes in Him and obeys Him put his trust, for we trust in Him and in Him we put our trust.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Then bring us a clear authority, he said: The clear authority is the proof and evidence. And his statement: (For which He has not sent down any authority), he said: Clear evidence and proof.

x: The Almighty says, informing about what the messengers said to their nations: And why should we not put our trust in God, trusting in Him and in His sufficiency and His defense of you from Him, while He has guided us to our ways, meaning: He has shown us the path of salvation from His punishment, so He has made it clear to us, and we will be patient over what you have harmed us, in God, and over what we encounter from you of hardship in Him because of our calling you to what we call you to, of disavowal of idols and statues, and sincerity in worship of Him, and in God let the trustful put their trust, meaning: and in God let everyone who has confidence in Him among His creation put their trust, but as for the one who disbelieves in Him, then his guardian is Satan.

God Almighty said: “And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, ‘We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion.’ So their Lord inspired to them, ‘We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.’”

God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God said to His messengers who were sent to them, when they called them to the oneness of God and to sincere worship of Him, and to abandon the worship of gods and idols, We will surely expel you from our land, meaning: from our country, so we will expel you from it, or you must return to our religion, meaning: unless you return to our religion that we follow, which is the worship of idols. And I inserted in his saying: You will surely return, the letter lam, which is in the sense of a condition, as if it were an answer to the oath. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: We will expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion. The meaning of or here is the meaning of except: or means until as is said in speech: I will hit you or you confess to me. Some Arabs make what comes after or in such a place an apposition to what comes before it.

If what comes before it is in the jussive mood, they make it in the jussive mood, and if it is in the accusative mood, they make it in the accusative mood. If it contains a lam they make a lam in it, since or is a conjunction.

Some of them make what comes after or in the accusative case in every case, so that it is known by its accusative that it is disconnected from the first and from what comes before it, as Imru’ al-Qais said: My friend cried when he saw the path before him and realized that we were following Caesar. I said to him: Do not cry, we are only trying to become king or die and be excused. So he put the word we die, so we can apologize, and he raised the word we try, because he wanted the meaning: unless we die, or until we die. And from this is the saying of the other: I cannot be separated from her affection, nor can love do to me anything other than what it did And His statement: Then their Lord inspired to them, ‘We will surely destroy the wrongdoers,’ those who wronged themselves, and thus deserved God’s punishment for them through their disbelief. It may be possible that they were called the wrongdoers because they worshipped idols and deities that it is not permissible to worship, so it was because they placed worship in the wrong place, since it was wrong, and they were called that.
And His statement:
h
And We will surely inhabit you in the land after them

, this is a promise from God to one of His prophets who promised victory over the disbelievers among his people. He says: When the nations of the messengers persisted in their disbelief, and threatened their messengers with attacking them, God revealed to them the destruction of those of their nations who disbelieved in them, and promised them victory. All of that was from God as a threat and a warning to the polytheists of the people of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for their disbelief in Him, and their boldness against His Prophet, and to strengthen Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to command him to be patient with the hardships he encountered from the polytheists of his people, just as those of His messengers who were before him were patient, and to know that the consequence of the matter of those who disbelieved in Him is destruction, and its consequence is victory over them, the way of God with those who passed away before.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We will surely settle you in the land after them, he said: He promised them victory in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter. And His saying: That is for him who fears standing before Me and fears My threat, the Most High says: This is what I do for him who fears standing before Me and fears My threat, so he fears Me through his obedience and avoids My wrath. I will support him against whatever evil he wants for him and whatever he seeks to do to him that is disliked by My enemies. I will destroy his enemy and disgrace him, and cause him to inherit his own harm and his own home. He said: For he who fears standing before Me, and its meaning is what I said: that it is for he who fears standing before Me, such that I will raise him there for the reckoning, just as He said: And you make your provision that you lie, meaning: And you make My provision that you lie. This is because the Arabs attribute their actions to themselves, and to what they have been done to, so they say: I was pleased to see you, and to see you, and so it is.

x: God Almighty says: And the messengers sought victory over their people, meaning they sought God’s help against them,
h
and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed

, meaning: every arrogant, unjust person who deviated from the acknowledgement of God’s oneness and the sincerity of worship to Him perished. Stubborn, obstinate and obstinate, they mean the same thing. And from the tyrant, he says: He is a tyrant between determinism, determinism, tyranny, tyranny, and tyranny. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us
m: - and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And seek victory, he said: All the messengers, he said: seek help, stubborn, he said: One who opposes the truth and deviates from it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sought victory
, he said: All the messengers sought victory,
h
And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed
, he said: One who opposes the truth and deviates from it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, and Ibn Jurayj said: They sought victory over their people.
Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us....

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they sought victory

, but every obstinate tyrant was disappointed. He said: The messengers and the believers were oppressed by their people, and they were subjugated by them and they were called to return to their religion, but God Almighty refused for His messengers and the believers to return to the religion of disbelief, and He commanded them to put their trust in God, and He commanded them to seek victory against the tyrants, and He promised them that He would inhabit the earth after them, so God fulfilled for them what He promised them,
h
and they sought victory
as He commanded them to seek victory,
h
and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And every obstinate tyrant will fail
, he said: He is the one who deviates from the truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Mutraf bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And every obstinate tyrant will fail
, he said: the one who deviates from the truth.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sought victory
, meaning: The messengers sought victory over their people. His statement:
h
And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed
, and the obstinate tyrant is the one who refused to say, There is no god but God.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they sought victory
, he said: The messengers sought victory over their people,
h
and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed
, he said: obstinate about the truth, turning away from it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly - and he added to it: he refused to say there is no god but God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And every obstinate tyrant will fail
, he said: The one who is obstinate about the truth, the one who turns away from the path, he said: And the Arabs say: The worst of people is the obstinate one, the one who deviates from the path.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sought victory

, but every obstinate tyrant was disappointed, he said: The tyrant is the arrogant. Ibn Zayd used to say about the meaning of his saying: And they asked for victory, contrary to what these people said, and he used to say: The nations asked for victory and were answered.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, And they asked for help, he said: Their asking for help was with a trial. They said, O God, if what Muhammad has brought is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained down upon the people of Lot, or bring us a painful punishment. He said: Their asking for help was with a trial as the people of Hud asked for help: Then bring upon us what You promise us, if you should be of the truthful. He said: The asking for help was with the punishment. He said: It was said to them: This has a term, when they asked God to send it down upon them, so He said: Rather, We will delay them until a day when eyes will stare in horror. They said: We do not want to be delayed until the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Our Lord, hasten for us our portion our punishment before the Day of Reckoning. And he recited: “And they urge You to hasten the punishment. And were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them” until he reached: And from beneath their feet and He will say, ‘Taste what you used to do.’

x: God Almighty says: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink from a purulent water.
God Almighty says: Behind him, in front of every tyrant, is Hell, they will return to it.

i: And behind in this place means: in front of you, as it is said: Death is behind you, meaning in front of you, and as the poet said:
x: You threaten me behind Bani Riyah? You lied. Your hands will fall short against me.
Meaning: behind Bani Riyah, in front of Bani Riyah and ahead of them.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: What he meant by his saying: behind it is in front of it, because it is behind what he is in, just as he says to you: All of this is behind you, meaning it will come upon you, and it is behind what you are in, because what you are in was before that and it is behind it. And he said: Behind them is a king who seizes every ship by force, from this meaning, meaning it was behind what they were in, in front of them.

Some of the Kufans used to say: This is most permissible at times, because time passes by you and becomes behind you if you pass it. Likewise and there was a king behind them, because they pass it and it becomes behind them.

Some of them said: It is one of the letters of opposites, meaning behind, it can be in front and behind. And his saying: And he is given to drink from pus-filled water, he says: And he is given to drink from water, then he explained that water, solved its praise and what it is, so he said: It is pus, and for that reason he returned pus in its parsing to water, because it is an explanation of it. Pus is blood and pus. And the people of interpretation interpreted it as well.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us
m: - and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: from pus-filled fluid, he said: pus and blood.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he is given to drink from a water of pus
, and pus is what flows from his flesh and skin.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And he is given to drink from a fluid of pus, he said: What flows from between his flesh and his skin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
h
And he is given to drink from a water of pus

, he said: He means by pus what comes out of the belly of the unbeliever, mixed with pus and blood. His saying: He sips it, means he drinks it, but he can hardly swallow it, means he can hardly swallow it because of the intensity of his dislike of it, and he can swallow it because of the intensity of his thirst. The Arabs use la yakad for both what he did and what he did not do. As for what he did, this is part of it, because God Almighty made that a drink for them. As for what he did not do, and kad is included in it, his saying: until when he put out his hand, he could hardly see it means he does not see it. In the same way as we said, the meaning of his saying: and he can hardly swallow it, and he swallows it, the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The novel mentioned that:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibrahim Abu Ishaq al-Talaqani told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Busr, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And he will be given to drink of a boiling water, gulping it down, so when he drinks it, it will cut up his intestines until it comes out of his anus. God Almighty says: And they will be given to drink scalding water, so it will cut up their intestines, and He says: “And if they call for help, they will be given water like molten brass, which will scald their faces. What an evil drink!”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, he said, Sufyan Ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Ubaid God Ibn Busr, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And they are given to drink from a boiling water, so he mentioned something similar, except that he said: They are given to drink scalding water.

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told me, he said, Haywah bin Shureih Al-Himsi told us, he said, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, he said, Ubaid God bin Busr told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. And his saying:
h
And death will come to him from every side

, but he is not dead, he is saying: And death will come to him from before him and from behind him, and from his right and his left, and from every part of his body, and he is not dead, because his soul does not leave him so he dies and finds rest, and he does not come back to life because his soul is attached to the throats, so it does not return to its place, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: He swallows it but can hardly swallow it, and death comes to him from every side, but he is not dead, he said: His soul is stuck at his throat, and it does not exit his mouth so he dies, nor does it return to its place in his body, so he finds comfort in that, and life benefits him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said: Yazid bin Harun told us, he said: Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And death will come to him from every side

, he said: from under every hair on his body. His saying: And behind him is a severe punishment, means: And behind what he is in of punishment, meaning in front of him and in front of him, is a severe punishment.

x: The Arab scholars differed about the raising of the word like.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is as if he said: And among what He has related to you is the example of those who disbelieved, then he began to explain, as he said: The example of Paradise, and this is common.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The example is for deeds, but the Arabs put the names first because they are more definite, then they bring the report that they are telling about with its owner. The meaning of the statement is: The example of the deeds of those who disbelieved in their Lord is like ashes, as it was said: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces will be blackened and the meaning of the statement is: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied about God, blackened. He said: If the deeds were lowered, it would be permissible, as he said: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month and his saying: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is that rivers flow beneath it He said: So flowing is in the place of the report, as if he said: that it flows, and that it is such and such, so if he had introduced that, it would have been permissible.

He said: And with it the saying of the poet: Leave me alone, for your command will not be obeyed, and you will not find my patience doubled. He said: So the dream is in the accusative case with I found for repetition. He said: If it had been raised, it would have been correct. He said: This is a parable that God gave for the deeds of the disbelievers. He said: The example of the deeds of those who disbelieved on the Day of Resurrection, which they used to do in this world, claiming that they intended God by them, is like ashes that the wind blows over on a stormy day, blowing them away and taking them away. So too are the deeds of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. They will not find anything of them that will benefit them with God and save them from His punishment, because they did not do them purely for God, but rather they associated idols and statues in them. God Almighty says:
h
That is the farthest error

, meaning that the deeds they did in this world, in which they associated partners with God, are deeds done without guidance and righteousness, rather, they were far from guidance and were taken without righteousness.

It was said: On a stormy day, so the day was described as stormy, which is a description of the wind, because the wind is in it, just as it is said: a cold day, and a hot day, because the cold and heat are in it, and as the poet said: Two cloudy days and one sunny day He described the two days as cloudy, and the clouds are in them. It may be possible that what was meant by it was: on a windy day, so the wind was omitted, because it was mentioned before that, so that would be similar to the poet’s saying: If a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed He means: the eclipse of the sun. It was said: It is a description of the wind specifically, but when it came after the day, its inflection was followed, and that is because the Arabs follow the genitive case with the genitive case in descriptions, as the poet said: You will see a smooth, flawless face with no blemishes or scars. So it was lowered not in accordance with the parsing of the face, but rather it is from the description of the year, and the meaning is: the year of the face is not disgusting, as they said: This is the hole of a ruined lizard.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like ashes that the wind blows violently
, he said: The wind carried it on a stormy day.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows fiercely on a stormy day

. He says: Those who disbelieved in their Lord and worshipped other than Him, their deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be like ashes which the wind blows fiercely on a stormy day. They will not be able to do anything of their deeds that will benefit them, just as ashes are not able to be done if they are sent down on a stormy day. Surat Ibrahim 14:18 The parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They will not be able to do anything of what they have earned. That is the extreme error. His saying:
h
That is the farthest error
, meaning the clear error, far from the path of truth.

x: God Almighty says: Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.

The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, and learned that God created the heavens and the earth with truth, alone in creating them, without support or helper, If He wills, He can take you away and bring forth a new creation, meaning: The One who is alone in creating and creating that without help or partner, if He wills to take you away and annihilate you, He will take you away and annihilate you, and bring forth another creation other than you in your place, and their creation will be barren, and that is not difficult for God, meaning: And your taking away and annihilating you and bringing forth another creation other than you in your place is not impossible or impossible for God, because He is able to do whatever He wills. The readers differed in the reading of his saying: Have you not seen that God created? This was read by most of the people of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians: Khalaq on the pattern of fa’l. The general reading of the people of Kufa is: Creator, on the active form. They are two widespread readings, each of which has been read by imams of the Qur’anic recitations, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The readers differed in the reading of his saying: Have you not seen that God created?
This was read by most of the people of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians: Khalaq on the pattern of fa’l.
The general reading of the people of Kufa is: Creator, on the active form.
They are two widespread readings, each of which has been read by imams of the Qur’anic recitations, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And they will all come forth before God

, that those who disbelieved in Him will appear on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, and they will be removed from the earth, all together, meaning all of them, Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, meaning the followers among them will say to those who were led, and they are those who were arrogant in this world about sincerely worshipping God and following the messengers who were sent to them, Indeed, we were your followers, in this world. The word tabi’a is the plural of tabi’a just as ghayb is the plural of ghayb. What they meant by their saying: We were your followers is that they were their followers in this world, obeying what they commanded them to do of worshipping idols and disbelieving in God, and refraining from what they forbade them from doing of following the Messengers of God.
So can you protect us from the punishment of God in any way? They mean: So can you protect us today from the punishment of God in any way?
Ibn Jurayj used to say something like this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: Then the weak said, he said: the followers, to those who were arrogant, he said: to the leaders. And His statement:
h
If God had guided us
, we would have guided you, the Almighty says: The leaders of disbelief in God said to their followers:
h
If God had guided us

, meaning: If God had made clear to us something by which we could repel His punishment from us today, we would have guided you, we would have responded to you so that you could repel the punishment from yourselves, but we were impatient with the punishment, so our impatientness and patience with it did not benefit us, It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient; there is no escape for us, meaning: they have no way out from it. It is said: He avoided something, if he turned away from it, he avoided ...

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Omar bin Abi Laila,
m: one of the Banu Amir, who said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say: It has reached me, or it was mentioned to me, that the people of Hell said to one another: O people, indeed what you see has befallen you of torment and calamity, so come, let us be patient, perhaps patience will benefit us, just as the people of this world were patient in obeying God, and patience benefited them when they were patient. He said: So they agreed on patience. He said: So they were patient, and their patience lasted a long time, then they became impatient and called out: It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient, there is no escape for us, meaning: no place of escape.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient

; there is no escape for us, he said: The people of Hell said to each other: Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise through their weeping and supplication to God, so come, let us weep and supplicate to God. He said: So they wept, and when they saw that it did not benefit them, they said: Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise through patience, come, let us be patient. So they were patient with a patience the like of which had never been seen, but that did not benefit them, so at that point they said:
h
It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient
; there is no escape for us.

x: God Almighty says: And Iblis said, When the matter was decided, meaning when the people of Paradise entered Paradise and the people of Hell entered Hell, and each group of them settled down: God promised you, O followers, Hell, and I promised you victory, but I broke my promise to you, and God fulfilled His promise to you,
h
and I had no authority over you

, meaning: And I had no argument over you, in what I promised you of victory, that would prove to me against you the truth of my words, except that I called you, and this is from the exception disconnected from the first, as you say: I did not hit him except because he was an idiot, and its meaning is: But I called you and you responded to me. He says: Except that I called you to obey me and disobey God, and you responded to my call, so do not blame me, for your response to me, but blame yourselves, for it,
h
I am not your savior
, he says:
h
I am not your savior

, nor are you my savior, nor are you my savior from God’s punishment or my deliverer from it, I disbelieved in what you associated before, he says: I denied that I was a partner with God in what you associated with me in your worship, before, in this world, indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment, he says: Indeed, for the disbelievers in God is a painful punishment from God, painful.

It is said: I made the man cry out if I helped him, by screaming, and the screamer screamed, screams, and screams, rarely, and it is the frank and the screaming. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer,
m: regarding this verse: “
h
I am not your savior

, nor are you my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Me before,” he said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection, Satan and Jesus, son of Mary. As for Satan, he will stand with his party and say this statement. As for Jesus, peace be upon him, he will say: “I did not say to them except what You commanded me, ‘Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.’ And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are Witness over all things.”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Two preachers will stand on the Day of Resurrection, one of them is Jesus and the other is Satan. As for Satan, he will stand with his party and say: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth. So David recited until he reached: Because you associated others with Him before. I do not know whether he completed the verse or not. As for Jesus, peace be upon him, it will be said to him: Did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as gods besides God?’ So he recited until he reached: Indeed, it is you who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated, Ali bin Asim narrated, on the authority of Dawud bin Hind, on the authority of Amer, who said: Two preachers will stand before the people on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty will say: O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as gods besides God?’ until His saying:
h
This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness

. He said: And Satan will stand and say: “I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior.” I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior.

c: Al-Husayn told us, Saeed bin Mansour told us, Khalid told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I am not your savior

, nor are you my savior, he said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection. As for Iblis, he will say this, and as for Jesus, he will say: I only said to them what You commanded me. Al-Muthanna narrated, Suwaid bin Nasr narrated, Ibn Al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Saad, who said:

c: Abd Al-Rahman bin Ziyad informed me, on the authority of Dukhayn Al-Hijri, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who mentioned the hadith, he said: Jesus says: That is the unlettered prophet. Then they come to me, and God gives me permission to stand, and from my seat rises the most fragrant odor that anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord, and He intercedes for me, and He gives me light upon light, from the hair of my head to the nails of my feet. Then the disbelievers say: The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so stand up and intercede for us, for you led us astray. Then he stands, and from his seat rises the most foul odor that anyone has ever smelled, then he glorifies Hell, and he says at that time: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And I had no authority over you

, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Satan will stand as a preacher on a pulpit of fire and say: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you, until His statement: And you are not my helpers, he said: My supporters, Indeed, I disbelieve in what you associated with Him before, he said: In your obedience to Me in this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned him, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say regarding His statement:
h
And Satan said

, when the matter has been decided, ‘Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth,’ he said: Iblis stood up to address them and said: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, until His statement:
h
I cannot help you
, meaning:
h
I cannot help you

at all, “nor can you help me. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before,” he said: So when they heard his statement, they hated themselves. He said: Then they were called out: And the hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves Al-Anʿam 2:17.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I am not your savior
, nor are you my savior, meaning I am not your helper, nor are you my helper. His statement: Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with Him before, meaning I disobeyed God before you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “I will not be your savior, nor will you be my savior. Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with Him before,” he said: This is the saying of Satan on the Day of Resurrection, he says: You will not be of any benefit to me, nor will I be of any benefit to you. Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with Him before, he said: His association, His worship.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: By my cry, he said: By my helper.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, who said:
m: I will not save you, and you will not be saved.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: He said: The truthful evil orator is Satan. Have you seen a truthful person who is not benefited by his truthfulness? “Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you.
h
And I had no authority over you
except that I invited you and you responded to me,” he said: You obeyed me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves, when you obeyed me.
h
I am not your savior

, I am not your helper or your supporter. And you are not my savior, you are not my helper or my supporter of what is in me. “Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with me before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Laila,
m: one of the Banu Amir, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say:
h
And Satan said

when the matter was decided, he said: Satan stood up at that time, meaning when the people of Hell said: It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient; there is no escape for us, so he addressed them and said: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and failed you, until His saying:
h
I cannot help you
, meaning
h
I cannot help you

at all, “nor can you help me. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before.” He said: So when they heard his words, they hated themselves. He said: Then they were called out: The hatred of God is greater than your hatred al-Anʿam 2:11.

x: God Almighty says: “And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’”
God Almighty said: Have you not seen how God presents an example? A good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and its branches reach the sky.

God Almighty says: And He admits those who believed in God and His Messenger, so they acknowledged the Oneness of God and the message of His Messengers, and that what they brought from God is true, and did righteous deeds, meaning: and they acted in obedience to God, so they adhered to God’s command and prohibition, to gardens beneath which rivers flow, orchards beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein, meaning: they will not remain therein forever, by permission of their Lord, meaning: they entered it by God’s command to them to enter, “their greeting therein is, ‘Peace,’” and that is, God willing, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: regarding his statement: “Their greeting therein is ‘Peace,’” he said: The angels greet them in Paradise. And His statement: “Have you not seen how God presents a parable:
h
a good word

is like a good tree,” the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, so that you may know how God has presented a parable and likened a likeness,
h
a good word

, meaning by goodness faith in Him, may He be glorified, like a tree with good fruit. He left out mentioning the fruit so that the listeners would not need to mention it by mentioning the tree. And His statement: its root is firm and its branches are in the heaven, the Most High says: the root of this tree is firm in the earth, and its branch, which is its highest part, is in the heaven, meaning: high up toward the heaven. And His statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord

, meaning: It feeds what is eaten from its fruit at all times by the command of its Lord. And God presents examples for the people, meaning: God presents examples for the people, and makes similarities appear to them, that they may remember, meaning: so that they may remember God’s proof against them, so that they may consider it and take heed, and so that they may turn away from their disbelief in Him and turn to faith.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the good word.
Some of them said: It means the faith of the believer.
Who said that?
