c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
A good word

, the testimony that there is no god but God, is like a good tree, which is the believer, its root is firm, he says: there is no god but God, firm in the heart of the believer, and its branches are in the heaven, he says: the believer’s deeds are raised by it to the heavens.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas:
m: h
A good word
, he said: This is an example of faith, so faith is a good tree, its firm root that does not fade is sincerity to God, and its branch is in the sky, its branch is the fear of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Mujahid said:
m: Have you not seen how God presents an example?
h
A good word

is like a good tree, he said: Like a palm tree. Ibn Jurayj said, and others said: The good word has a firm root, it has a foundation in the heart, and its branches are in the heaven, it ascends and is not veiled until it reaches God.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the believer himself.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: his saying: “Have you not considered how God presents a parable?
h
A good word

is like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches are in the heaven. It produces its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord.” By the good tree he means the believer, and by the root firmly fixed in the earth and by the branch in the heaven he means that the believer works on the earth and speaks, so his actions and words reach the heaven while he is on the earth.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
God sets forth a parable
h
a good word
is like a good tree,” he said: That is the parable of the believer, from whom good words and righteous deeds continue to come forth and ascend to him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, who said:
m: Its root is firmly fixed in the earth, and that is how he used to recite it. He said: That is the believer, he gave an example. He said: Sincerity to God alone and His worship, with no partner for Him. He said: Its root is firmly fixed, he said: The root of his work is firmly fixed in the earth, and its branch is in the heaven, he said: His remembrance is in the heaven. They differed about this tree that was made an example of
h
a good word
. Surat Ibrahim 14:25
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
. And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded.

x: Some of them said: It is the palm tree.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Muʿawiyah Ibn Qurrah, he said:
m: I heard Anas Ibn Malik regarding this word, like a good tree, he said: It is the palm tree.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abu Qatan told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of Anas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, he said:
m: I heard Anas bin Malik say:
h
A good word
is like a good tree, he said: the palm tree.

c: Yaqub and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Shuʿayb told us, he said:
m: I went out with Abu Al-ʿAliyah seeking Anas bin Malik, he said: So we came to him, and he called for us to have dates on it, and he said: Eat from this tree about which God Almighty said: “
h
God sets forth a parable
h
a good word
is like a good tree, whose root is firm and its branches reach to the sky,” and Al-Hasan said in his hadith: with a veil.

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said, Shuaib bin Al-Habhab told us, on the authority of Anas:
m: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a date palm, and he said: The parable of
h
a good word
is like a good tree. He said: It is the palm tree.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Shuʿayb bin Al-Habhab, on the authority of Anas:
m: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a veil containing dates, and he said: The parable of
h
a good word
is like a good tree. He said: It is the palm tree. Shuʿayb said: So I told Abu Al-ʿAliyah about that, and he said: That is what they used to say.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Shuʿayb bin Al-Habhab, he said:
m: We were with Anas, and a plate, or a basket, was brought to us, on which were dates. He said: Eat, O Abu Al-ʿAliyah, for this is from the tree that God Almighty mentioned in His Book: “God presents an example:
h
a good word
is like a good tree, whose root is firm.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Mahdi bin Maimun told me, on the authority of Shuʿayb bin Al-Habhab, he said:
m: Abu Al-ʿAliyah used to come to me. One day he came to my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, so I went with him to Anas bin Malik, and we entered with him to Anas bin Malik, and a plate was brought with dates on it. Anas said to Abu Al-ʿAliyah: Eat, O Abu Al-ʿAliyah, for this is from the tree of which God said in His Book: Have you not seen how God presents an example:
h
A good word
is like a good tree, whose root is firm. He said: This is how Anas recited it that day.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Talq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Ghaffar bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Jami’ bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Marra bin Sharahil Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Masruq:
m: Like a good tree, he said: the palm tree.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: like a good tree, he said: like a palm tree.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: like a good tree, he said: It is the palm tree, it always has benefits.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: like a good tree, he said: God gave the example of the believer like the palm tree, which yields its fruit at all times.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: The example of
h
a good word
is like a good tree, we used to say that it was the palm tree.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Like a good tree, he said: They claim that it is the palm tree.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times
, he said: It is the palm tree.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And its branches are in the sky
, he said: the palm trees.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
It yields its fruit every season
, he said: It is the palm tree.

c: Muhammad bin Al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said,
m: Shu’ayb bin Al-Habhab said, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: The good tree is the palm tree.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a tree in Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Abu Kudayna told us, he said, Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: “God presents a parable:
h
a good word
is like a good tree, whose root is firm
h
and its branches are in the sky
. It produces its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord,” he said: It is a tree in Paradise.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: It is the palm tree, due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which says:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: “I accompanied Ibn Umar to Madinah, and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except one hadith. He said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a date-palm tree was brought to him, and he said: ‘Among the trees is a tree the size of a Muslim man.’ I wanted to say that it is the palm tree, but I was the youngest of the people, so I kept quiet, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is the palm tree.’”

c: Al-Hasan told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Sarj, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what the good tree is? Ibn Umar said: I wanted to say: It is the palm tree, but Umar prevented me, so they said: God and His Messenger know best. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, Yahya bin Hammad told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to his companions: Is there a tree among the trees that does not shed its leaves like the believer? He said: So the people mentioned the trees of the desert, and it occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I was embarrassed, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Asim bin Ali told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Muslim Al-Qasmali told us, he said, Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Omar:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. So tell me what it is?’ So he mentioned something similar.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Ali told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Tell me about a tree like a Muslim man, it produces its fruit every season, and its leaves do not fall?” He said: It occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I hated to speak while Abu Bakr and Umar were there. When they did not speak, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Ismail told us, on the authority of Ubaid God, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the time that God Almighty mentioned in this place, saying: It produces its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord.
Some of them said: It means: It produces its fruit every morning and every day.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Now could be in the morning or the evening.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: Morning and evening.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Talq told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: In the morning and the evening.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: Morning and evening.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said,
m: my father told Surat Ibrahim 14:25
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
. And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded. me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: It remembers God at every hour of the night and day.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Abu Kudayna told us, he said, Qabus told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: morning and evening.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: The believer obeys God at night and during the day and at all times.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, his work ascends at the beginning and end of the day.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: His deeds ascend morning and evening.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
It brings forth its fruit at all times
, by permission of its Lord, that
h
it brings forth its fruit at all times
. This is like the believer who works at all times, every hour of the day and every hour of the night, in the winter and the summer, in obedience to God.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that
h
it bears fruit
every six months, from the time it is ripe until it is pregnant.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Tariq bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The time is six months.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, he said, Ikrimah said:
m: I was asked about a man who swore that he would not do such and such until a certain time? I said: There is a time when it is attained, and there is a time when it is not attained. The time when it is not attained is His statement:
h
And you will surely know its report after a while
, and the time when it is attained is:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: That is from the time the palm tree is cut down until the time it blossoms, and that is six months.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Asbahani, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Now, six months.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: It is the palm tree, and the time is six months.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Katheer bin Hisham told us, he said, Jaafar told us, he said, Ikrimah told us:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: It is the period between the date palm bearing fruit until it finds fruit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Ikrimah told us:
m: Now it is six months.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Tariq bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He was asked about a man who swore that he would not speak to his brother for a while. He said: A period of six months. Then he mentioned the palm tree, the period between its bearing and its harvesting is six months.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: h
It yields its fruit every season
, he said: six months.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It produces its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord. The time is between seven and six, and it is eaten in winter and summer.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: Between six and seven months, meaning now.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: The time is six months.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a year here now.

Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Wakiʿ narrated, on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of Ikrimah: That he vowed to cut off the hand of his slave or to imprison him for a while. He said: So Umar ibn Abdul Aziz asked me, he said: I said: Do not cut off his hand, and imprison him for a year, and the time is a year.
He will surely imprison him for a time, and he recited:
h
It brings forth its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Wakiʿ narrated, he said: When it is known and when it is not known. As for the time that is known, it is:
h
And you will surely know its report after a while
, and as for the time that is known, it is His statement:
h
It brings forth its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said:
m: I asked Hammad and Al-Hakam about a man who swore that he would not speak to a man for a while? He said: The period is one year.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, Al-Hasan told us, Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told me, and Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Every time, he said: Every year.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
It yields its fruit every season
, he said: every year.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Salam told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of a man among them:
m: He asked Ibn Abbas, saying: I swore that I would not speak to a man for a while? So Ibn Abbas read:
h
It yields its fruit at all times
, so a time is a year.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn Ghasil told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz sent for me and said: O client of Ibn Abbas, I swore that I would not do such and such for a while, so what is the time by which you will recognize it? I said: Of the times there is a time that is not realized, and of the times there is a time that is realized. As for the time that is not realized, it is the saying of God: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? By God, He does not know how long he had been there before he was created. As for the time that is realized, it is His saying:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, so it is between one year and the next year. So he said: You are right, O client of Ibn Abbas, how well you said it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I vowed not to speak to a man for a while. Ibn Abbas said:
h
It bears fruit
every time, so a time is a year.

x: Others said: Rather, it is now two months in this place.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Muslim al-Ta’ifi told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah, who said:
m: A man came to Saeed bin al-Musayyab and said: I swore that I would not speak to so-and-so for a while. He said: God Almighty said:
h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
. He said: It is the palm tree, and its fruit does not come out for more than two months, so two months are two months.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: “By ‘now’ in this place he meant morning and evening, and every hour, because God, the Most High, mentioned Him, made an example of what this tree produces at every moment of food for the work and speech of the believer. There is no doubt that the believer’s good deeds and speech are raised up to God every day, not every year, or every six months, or every two months. So if that is the case, then there is no doubt that the example does not differ in meaning from what it is used for. And if that is the case, then it is clear that what we have said is correct.
Which palm tree produces food at all times, summer and winter?
As for the winter, the pollen is from its food, and as for the summer, it produces dates, unripe dates, fresh dates, and dried dates, and all of that is from its food. And his saying: “
h
It bears fruit
,” is as follows:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, he said: Its fruit is eaten in the winter and the summer.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It yields its fruit at all times
, he said: It is eaten in winter and summer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas:
m: h
It brings forth its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord
, his work ascends, meaning work from the beginning of the day to its end.

evidence.text: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, who said: Its root is firmly fixed in the earth, and that is how he used to recite it.
He said: This is how Anas recited it that day.

x: God Almighty says: The example of associating partners with God, which is the evil word, is like a bad tree.
The people of interpretation differed about which tree it is? Most of them said: It is colocynth.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah, he said:
m: I heard Anas ibn Malik say about this verse: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, the artery. So I said: What is the artery? A man in his presence said: Colocynth, and Muʿawiyah acknowledged it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, he said:
m: I heard Anas bin Malik say: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, he said: Colocynth.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Amr bin Al-Haitham told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: The artery, meaning colocynth.

c: Ahmad bin Mansour told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Hubban bin Shu’bah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik,
m: regarding his statement: like a bad tree, he said: the artery. I said to Anas: What is the artery? He said: Colocynth.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Shuʿayb told us:
m: I went out with Abu al-ʿAliyah, intending to visit Anas ibn Malik, so we came to him, and he said: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, that is the colocynth.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Shuaib bin Al-Habhab, on the authority of Anas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Abu Iyas told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: The evil tree is the artery. So I said: What is the artery? He said: Colocynth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Shu’ayb, on the authority of Anas, he said:
m: That is colocynth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Mahdi bin Maimun told us, on the authority of Shuʿayb, he said, Anas said:
m: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, the verse. He said: That is colocynth. Have you not seen the winds, how they blow right and left?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Like a bad tree, colocynth.

x: Others said: This tree was not created on Earth.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za’farani told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Aw Kadina told us, he said, Qabus told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He said: This is an example that God gave, and this tree was not created on the face of the earth.

c: It was narrated from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that the statement of the one who said: It is colocynth is correct. If it is correct, then there is no statement that can be said other than it. Otherwise, it is a tree with the description that God described it with. Mentioning the report that we mentioned about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, my father told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Shuʿayb bin Al-Habhab, on the authority of Anas bin Malik,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of a bad word is that of a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He said: It is the colocynth. Shuʿayb said: I told that to Abu Al-ʿAliyah, and he said: That is what they used to say. His saying:
h
It was uprooted from the surface of the earth
, means: it was eradicated. It is said: I uprooted something, I uprooted it, if I eradicated it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Uprooted from the surface of the earth, he said:
h
It was uprooted from the surface of the earth

. It has no stability, meaning: This tree has no stability or root in the earth on which to stand and survive. This Surat Ibrahim 14:26 And the parable of an evil word is that of an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. tree, which God described with this description, was given as an example of the disbelief of the disbeliever and his association of partners with Him. He says: The disbelief of the disbeliever and his actions, which are disobedience to God, have no stability on earth, nor does it have a place to ascend to the heavens, because nothing of it ascends to God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the example of a bad word is that of a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. God gave the example of the bad tree as the example of the disbeliever. He says: The bad tree was uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He says: The disbeliever’s work is not accepted and he does not ascend to God, so he has no firm root on the earth, nor a branch in the heaven. He says: He has no good deeds in this world or in the hereafter.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the example of a bad word is that of a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth

, having no stability. Qatada said: A man met a man of knowledge and said: What do you say about a bad word? He said: I do not know of any place for it to settle on earth, nor any place for it to ascend to heaven, except that it clings to the neck of its owner until he meets it on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: “A man’s cloak was blown away by the wind, so he cursed it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not curse it, for it is commanded, and whoever curses something that is not worthy of it, the curse will return to its owner.” Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree. He said: This disbeliever has no deeds on earth, nor is he mentioned in heaven. Uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He said: His deeds do not ascend to heaven, nor do they remain on earth. It was said: Then where are their deeds? He said: They carry their burdens on their backs.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi:
m: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth. He said: The example of the disbeliever, no good word or righteous deed ascends to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: And the example of a bad word, which is polytheism, is like a bad tree, meaning the disbeliever. He said: Uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability, meaning: Polytheism has no basis for the disbeliever to follow, nor any proof, and God does not accept any action with polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And the example of a bad word is like that of a bad tree. He said: The example of a bad tree is like that of an unbeliever, whose words and deeds have no root or branch, and neither his words nor his deeds remain on the earth nor ascend to the heavens.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: God gave the example of the unbeliever: Like a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He said: It has no root or branch, no fruit, and no benefit. Likewise, the unbeliever does not do good nor say it, and God has not placed in him any blessing or benefit.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
God confirms those who believe

, God confirms their deeds and their faith, with the firm word, meaning: with the true word, which is, as it has been said, the testimony that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. As for his saying:
h
In this worldly life
, the people of interpretation differed about it.
Some of them said: What he meant by that is that God will establish them in their graves before the Day of Resurrection.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib Salim bin Janadah told me, he said, Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Sa'd bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Al-Bara' bin Azib,
m: regarding His statement,
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world

, he said: Confirmation in the life of this world is when the two angels come to him in the grave and say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. He says to him: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. They say to him: Who is your prophet? He says: My prophet Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him. So that is confirmation in the life of this world.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib,
m: with a similar meaning.

c: Abdullah bin Ishaq al-Naqid al-Wasiti told me, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ubaydah, on the authority of al-Bara’, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the believer and the disbeliever, and he said: When the believer is asked in his grave, he will say: My Lord is God. This is what He said:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik told us, Shuʿbah told us, Alqamah ibn Murthad told me,
m: I heard Saʿd ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of al-Baraʿ ibn ʿAzib: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When a Muslim is asked in the grave, he bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. He said: That is what God says: ‘
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter

c: Al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabsha and Muhammad ibn Muammar al-Bahrani told me
m: - and the wording is from the hadith of Ibn Abi Kabsha - they said: Abu Amir Abdul Malik ibn Amr told us, he said: Ibad ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saʿid, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at a funeral and he said: O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his companions disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a hammer in his hand and makes him sit and says: What do you say about this man? If he is a believer, he will say: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He will say to him: You have spoken the truth. A door to Hell will be opened for him and it will be said: This would have been your home had you disbelieved in your Lord, but since you believed in Him, God has replaced it with this. Then a door to Paradise will be opened for him and he will want to get up for it, but it will be said to him: Be still. Then his grave will be made spacious for him. As for the disbeliever or hypocrite, it will be said to him: What do you say? In this man? He will say: I do not know! It will be said to him: You neither knew nor were you able to learn nor were you guided! Then a door to Paradise will be opened for him and he will be told: This is your home if you had believed in your Lord. But since you disbelieved, God has replaced this for you. Then a door to Hell will be opened for him and the angel will strike him with a hammer so hard that all of God’s creation will hear it except the two heavy ones. Some of his companions said: O Messenger of God, there is not one of us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer but that he will be struck by it! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word
in this world and in the Hereafter,
h
and God leaves astray the wrongdoers
h
and God does what He wills

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’:
m: “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer: His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and make him sit - meaning in his grave - and they say: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. They say: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. They say to him: Who is this man who was sent among you? He says: He is the Surat Ibrahim 14:27
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter
h
And God leaves astray the wrongdoers
h
and God does what He wills

. Messenger of God. They say to him: How do you know? He says: I read the Book of God and I believed in it and confirmed it. Then a voice from the heaven calls out: My servant has told the truth.” He said: That is the saying of God, the Almighty:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, he said, Al-Munhal bin Amr told us, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, he said, Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said, Saeed ibn Mansur narrated to us, he said, Mahdi ibn Maimun narrated to us
m: - all of them, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer! He said: Then someone will come to him in his grave and say: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? He will say: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he will be rebuked and he will say: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? This is the last trial that will be presented to the believer, and that is when God the Almighty says: “God will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter,” and he will say: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then it will be said to him: You have spoken the truth.” - and the wording is from the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la.

c: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told us, Adam told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: God will keep firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. He said: That is when it is said in the grave: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? He says: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He came with clear proofs from God, so I believed in him and confirmed his faith. It is said to him: You have spoken the truth! Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be resurrected. Mujahid bin Musa and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated, Yazid narrated, Muhammad bin Amr narrated, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The dead person hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away from him. If he is a believer, the prayer is at his head, the zakat is on his right, and fasting is on his left. Good deeds such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, doing good deeds, and being kind to people are at his feet. He is approached from his head and the prayer says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached from his right and the zakat says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached from his left and fasting says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached from his feet and the good deeds such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, doing good deeds, and being kind to people say: There is no entrance before me. He is told: Sit down. He sits, and the sun appears to him as if it is about to set. He is told: Tell us about what we ask you. He says: Leave me until I pray. It will be said: You will do so, so tell us about what we ask you about! He will say: What are you asking about? It will be said: Did you see this man who was among you? What do you say about him, and what do you testify against him? He will say: Is he Muhammad? It will be said to him: Yes. He will say: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God, and that he came with clear proofs from God, so we believed him. It will be said to him: Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, God willing. Then his grave will be made seventy cubits deep and illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise will be opened for him and he will be told: Look at what has been prepared for you therein, so he will be even more delighted and happy. Then a door to the canine tooth will be opened for him and he will be told: Look at what God has diverted from you had you disobeyed Him! So he will be even more delighted and happy. Then his breath will be placed in the good breath, which is a green bird that clings to the trees of Paradise, and his body will be returned to the dust it was from. This is the saying of God:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Abu Qatan told us, Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mukhariq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: When a believer dies, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet? So God makes him firm and he says: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad. Then Abdullah recited:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Qurashi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father - and Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Al-Baraa,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life
, he said: The torment of the grave.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Al-Bara’, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter, Shu’bah said something that I did not remember. He said: In the grave.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word
, until His statement:
h
And God leaves astray the wrongdoers

, he said: When death approaches a believer, the angels attend him, greet him, and give him good tidings of Paradise. Then when he dies, they walk in his funeral procession and pray over him with the people. Then when he is buried, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. And it is said to him: Who is your Messenger? He says: Muhammad. And it is said to him: What is your testimony? He says: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Then his grave is expanded for him as far as his sight can reach.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, I heard Ibn Tawus narrating, on the authority of his father, he said: I do not know him except that he said: It is in the trial of the grave, in His statement:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father,
m: that he used to say about this verse:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter, it is about the owner of the grave.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’:
m: h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter, he said: It was revealed about the occupant of the grave.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter, he said: It has reached us that this nation will be questioned in their graves, and God will confirm the believer in his grave when he is questioned.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Rabia Fahd told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer, he said: Then his soul returns to his body, and God sends to him two angels who are very severe in their rebuke, and they make him sit and rebuke him, saying: Who is your Lord? He said: He says: God. And what is your religion? He said: Islam. He said: They say to him: Who is this man, or prophet, who was sent among you? He says: Muhammad is the Messenger of God. He said: They say to him: How do you know? He says: I read the Book of God and believed in it and confirmed it!” That is the saying of God:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter
, he said: It was revealed regarding the dead person who is asked in his grave about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
and in the Hereafter, he said: It has reached us that this nation will be questioned in their graves, and God will confirm the believer where he is questioned.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life
, he said: This is in the grave, he is addressed, and in the afterlife it is the same.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
God confirms those who believe
in faith
h
in this worldly life
, which is the established statement, and in the Hereafter, the issue is in the grave.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
, he said: There is no god but God, and in the Hereafter, the questioning in the grave.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world
. As for the life of this world, He confirms them with goodness and righteous deeds. And his statement: and in the Hereafter, meaning in the grave. Surat Ibrahim 14:27
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter
h
And God leaves astray the wrongdoers
h
and God does what He wills

x: The correct statement regarding this is what was proven by the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this, which is that its meaning is:
h
God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world

, and that is His confirmation of them in the life of this world through belief in God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Hereafter, with the same as He confirmed them with in the life of this world, and that is in their graves when they are asked about what they were upon of monotheism and belief in His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for his saying: And God misguides the wrongdoers, it means that God does not grant success to the hypocrite and the disbeliever
h
in this worldly life
and in the Hereafter when questioned in the grave, because of what the believer has been guided to in terms of faith in God and His Messenger.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: As for the disbeliever, the angels descend when death approaches him, and they spread out their hands - spreading means striking - they strike their faces and backs at death. Then when he is put in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He does not respond to them at all, and God makes him forget to mention that. And when it is said to him: Who is the Messenger who was sent to you? He does not find guidance for him, and does not respond to him at all. God says:
h
And God leaves astray the wrongdoers

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Fahd bin Awf Abu Rabia told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned the disbeliever when his soul is taken, he said: Then his soul is returned to his body. He said: Then two angels come to him who are very harsh, and they make him sit and rebuke him, and they say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: I do not know. He said: Then they say to him: What is your religion? He says: I do not know. He said: Then it is said to him: Who is this prophet who was sent among you? He says: I heard the people say that, I do not know. He said: Then they say: I did not know. He said: And that is the saying of God: “
h
And God leaves astray the wrongdoers
h
and God does what He wills
.” And His saying:
h
And God does what He wills

, meaning, by that, the Most High, the Most Majestic, means: And in God’s hand is guidance and misguidance, so do not deny, O people, His power, nor the guidance of those among you who are astray, nor the misguidance of those among you who are guided, for in His hand is the management of His creation and the turning of their hearts, and He does with them what He wills.

x: God Almighty says: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin?

God the Almighty says: Have you not looked, O Muhammad, at those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? He says: They changed the favors that God bestowed upon them, and made them disbelieve in Him. Their exchange of the favor of God for disbelief in the Prophet of God Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God bestowed him upon the Quraysh, then expelled him from them, and sent him among them as a Messenger of mercy to them, and a favor from Him to them, but they disbelieved in him and denied him, so they exchanged the favor of God upon them for disbelief. And His statement:
h
And they made their people dwell in the abode of ruin
, He says: And they made their people, the polytheists of Quraysh, dwell in the abode of ruin, which is
h
the abode of destruction

. It is said from this: something became bara yaburan, meaning it was destroyed and nullified. From this is the statement of Ibn al-Zubayri, and it has been said that it is from Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib: O Messenger of the King, my tongue is mending what I have torn when I was in a coma.
Then he translated about
h
the abode of destruction

, and what it is, and it was said: Hell they will enter, and what an evil resting place it is, meaning: And what an evil resting place it is for those who enter it. And it was said: Those who exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief: Banu Umayyah and Banu Makhzum.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Saʿd, on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction

, Hell? He said: They are the two most wicked of the Quraysh 106:Banu al-Mughira and Banu Umayya. As for Banu al-Mughira, you spared them on the day of Badr, but as for Banu Umayya, they were given respite for a time.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us: Hamza Al-Zayyat told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas said to Umar, may God be pleased with them both: O Commander of the Faithful, this verse, Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin, he said: They are the two most wicked of Quraysh, my maternal uncles and your paternal uncles. As for my maternal uncles, God eradicated them on the day of Badr, and as for your paternal uncles, God granted them respite for a time.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr Dhi Murr, on the authority of Ali:
m: h
And they made their people dwell in the abode of ruin
. He said: The two wicked ones from Quraysh.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr Dhi Murr, on the authority of Ali,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan and Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr Dhi Murr, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction
? He said: Banu al-Mughira and Banu Umayya. As for Banu al-Mughira, God cut off their roots on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayya, they were granted enjoyment for a time.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, he said: I heard ʿAli say about this verse:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
? He said: The two wicked ones from Banu Asad and Banu Makhzum.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayfil, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: They are the infidels of Quraysh, meaning in his statement:
h
And they made their people dwell in the home of destruction
, Hell.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayyal,
m: that he heard Ali Ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn Al-Kawwa asked him about this verse:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction
? He said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Badr.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Al-Nadr Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, who said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Tayyal, who said: I heard Ali, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Abu Art’ah, on the authority of Ali, regarding his statement:
h
Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief
? He said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh. This is what Abu Al-Sa’ib Muslim Al-Batin said, on the authority of Abu Art’ah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za’farani told us: Abu Mu’awiyah Al-Dharee’ told us: Ismail bin Samee’ told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Arta’ah, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding the Almighty’s statement: Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief, he said: The disbelievers of Quraysh.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yaqub bin Ishaq told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Bazza, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayyal, on the authority of Ali, who said
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
? He said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, who said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Tayyal narrating, who said: I heard Ali say about this verse:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction
? He said: The infidels of Quraysh on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us: Bassam Al-Sayrafi told us: Abu Al-Tayfil Amer bin Wathilah told us:
m: Ali stood on the pulpit and said: Ask me before you do not ask me, and you will not ask anyone like me after me. Then Ibn Al-Kawwa stood up and said: Who are those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? He said: The hypocrites of Quraysh.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Bassam told us, on the authority of a man named by Al-Tanafisi, who said:
m: A man came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? He said: Among the Quraysh.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Bassam Al-Sayrafi told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayfil, on the authority of Ali,
m: that he was asked about this verse: Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief. He said: The hypocrites of Quraysh.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Affan told us: Hammad told us: Amr bin Dinar told us that Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they made their people dwell in the home of destruction
, he said: They are the polytheists of the people of Badr.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abdul-Jabbar told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, who said:
m: I heard Ata’ say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: By God, they are the people of Mecca who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Hasan narrated: Salih bin Umar narrated: Mutraf bin Tarif narrated: Abu Ishaq narrated: I heard Umar bin Tarif say: I heard Ali say on the pulpit, and he recited this verse:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
? He said: They are the two most wicked of Quraysh. As for one of them, God cut off their roots on the day of Badr, and as for the other, they were given enjoyment for a time.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
m: - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us - and Al-Hasan told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
They exchanged the favor of God for disbelief
, he said: The disbelievers of Quraysh.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The infidels of Quraysh.

c: Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They exchanged the favor of God for disbelief
, the infidels of Quraysh.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: By God, they are those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin, the Quraysh, or he said: the people of Mecca.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Bashar told us: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding this verse, Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction, he said: Those killed on the day of Badr.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction, he said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: They are the polytheists killed at Badr.
b.via: Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding
h
those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
, he said: By God, they are the people of Mecca. Abu Kurayb said: Sufyan said: He means their disbelievers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they made their people dwell in the home of destruction
, he said: They are the polytheists of the people of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of some of the companions of Ali, on the authority of Surat Ibrahim 14:
m: 29 Hell they will burn in it, and wretched is the resting place. Ali, regarding his statement:
h
Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief

? He said: They are the two wicked ones from Quraysh, from Banu Makhzum and Banu Umayyah. As for Banu Makhzum, God cut off their roots on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayyah, they were granted respite for a time.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ma’la bin Asad told us: Khalid told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief
? He said: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: They are the infidels of Quraysh who were killed at Badr.
b.via: Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said:
m: They are the infidels of Quraysh, those who were killed at Badr.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief
?... the verse, he said: They are the polytheists of Mecca.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, who said:
m: This verse was revealed about those who were killed from Quraysh 106:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction
?... the verse.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
? We were told that they were the people of Mecca: Abu Jahl and his companions whom God killed on the day of Badr. God said, Hell they will burn in it, and wretched is the resting place.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they made their people dwell in the home of destruction
, he said: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr. They made their people dwell in the home of destruction, Hell, which they will burn in.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin
, he said: These are the polytheists from the people of Badr.

x: Others said about this, including:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction

, Hell, which they will burn in? He is Jabalah bin Al-Ayham, and those among the Arabs who followed him joined the Romans. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: And they made their people dwell in the house of destruction, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And they made their people dwell in
h
the abode of destruction
. He said: They made those of their people who obeyed them dwell in it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The abode of ruin, he said: Destruction, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said:
h
And they made their people dwell in the abode of ruin
, he said: The companions of Badr.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
The abode of destruction
, meaning the Fire, he said: And God has made that clear and informed you of it? He said: Hell, they will burn in it, and wretched is the resting place.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The abode of destruction
, Hell, they will burn in it. It is their abode in the afterlife.

evidence.text: Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Hasan narrated: Salih bin Umar narrated: Mutraf bin Tarif narrated: Abu Ishaq narrated: I heard Umar bin Tarif say: I heard Ali say on the pulpit, and he recited this verse: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin?

x: God Almighty says: And those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief have made rivals to their Lord. It is the plural of peer, and I have explained the meaning of peer in what has passed with its evidence in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. Rather, what He meant is that they made partners for God.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And they have made rivals to God

, and rivals are partners. And his statement: that they may lead astray from His path, the readings differed in your reading. The majority of the Kufic readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that they may lead people astray from the path of God by what they did of that. The majority of the Basran readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that people may be led astray from the path of God by what they did of that. The majority of the Basran readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that those who make rivals to God may be led astray from the path of God. And His saying, Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves,’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Enjoy yourselves in the life of this world, as a warning from God to them, not permitting them to enjoy it, nor as an order in the manner of worship, but as a rebuke, threat, and warning. And He made that clear with His saying, Then your destination is the Fire, meaning: Enjoy yourselves in the life of this world, for it will quickly pass away from you, and you will soon be in the Fire, and there you will know after your enjoyment in this world through your disobedience to God and your disbelief in Him therein.

evidence.text: And his statement: that they may lead astray from His path, the readings differed in your reading.
The majority of the Kufic readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that they may lead people astray from the path of God by what they did of that.
The majority of the Basran readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that people may be led astray from the path of God by what they did of that.
The majority of the Basran readers read it li-yidilu, meaning: so that those who make rivals to God may be led astray from the path of God.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to My servants who have believed in you, and have believed that what I have brought them is from Me, to establish prayer, meaning: Tell them: Let them establish the five obligatory prayers within their limits, and let them spend from what We have provided them, for We have granted them from Our bounty secretly and openly, so let them fulfill what We have obligated upon them of rights therein secretly and openly, before a Day comes in which there is no exchange, meaning: no ransom or compensation will be accepted from a soul that is obligated to be punished by God for its disobedience to its Lord in this world, so the ransom is accepted from it, and it is left and not punished, so God, may He be glorified and praised, called the ransom a compensation, since We take compensation from someone who is being compensated.

And his saying, nor friendship, means: There is no friendship of a friend, so he forgives the one who deserves punishment for his friendship, rather there is justice and equity, so friendship is a source of the saying of the speaker: I was friends with so-and-so, so I am friends with him through friendship and friendship, and from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: I turned away my love from them for fear of ruin, and I am not able to do good deeds or bad deeds. His statement, establish prayer, is interpreted as a consequence, and its meaning is: the command, meaning tell them to establish prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abdullah told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer, meaning the five daily prayers, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, meaning the zakat on their wealth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Before a Day comes in which there will be no trading or friendship

, Qatada said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, knows that in this world there are trading and friendships in this world, so a man should consider who he will befriend and what he will befriend. If it is for God, then let him continue, but if it is for other than God, then it will come to an end.

x: God the Almighty says: God is He who created the heavens and the earth from nothing, O people, and sent down from the sky rain with which He revived the trees and crops, so they produced sustenance for you that you may eat. And He has subjected to you the ships - which are the ships - to sail through the sea by His command - for you to ride them, and to carry your belongings in them from one country to another.
h
And He has subjected to you the rivers

- whose water is a drink for you. God the Almighty says: The One who deserves your worship and sincere obedience to Him is the one of this description, not the one who is not able to harm or benefit himself or anyone else from your idols, O polytheists, and your gods.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, meaning Al-Za’farani, told us: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And He has subjected to you the rivers
, he said: In every town.

x: God Almighty says, God is He who created the heavens and the earth and performed the actions that He described, and has subjected to you the sun and the moon, they alternate with you, O people, by night and by day, for the betterment of your souls and your livelihood, constantly in their alternation with you, and it was said: its meaning is: that they are constant in obeying God.

c: Khalaf bin Wasil told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon
, both diligently pursuing their courses, he said: Their diligence in obeying God. And His saying:
h
And He has subjected to you the night and the day they differ for you in succession

. If one goes, the other comes with your benefits and the improvement of your causes. So this is for you to use it for your livelihood, and this is for you to dwell in, you dwell in it, and as a mercy from Him to you.

x: God the Most High says: And He gave you, along with His favor upon you, what He bestowed upon you of the subjection of these things that He subjected to you and the provision that He provided you with from the plants and crops of the earth, from everything that you asked for and desired something from, and the second thing was omitted because what was added to it is all, and it was only permissible to omit it because of the particle of what comes after it, so it was sufficient by its indication of the particle of the object, so it was permissible to omit it, and similar to it is His statement, the Most High: And I was given of everything meaning by it: And I was given of everything in its time. And it was said: That was only said for the sake of multiplication, like the saying of the speaker: So-and-so knows everything, and all the people came to him, and he means some of them, and likewise His statement We opened for them the doors of everything and it was also said: That there is nothing except that some of the people asked it, so it was said: And He gave you of everything that you asked Him, meaning that He gave some of you something from it, and He gave another something of what he had asked for.
This is what some grammarians of Basra say.
