Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: Its meaning is: And He gave you everything you asked for if you asked Him, as if it was said: And He gave you everything you asked for, and he said: Do you not see that you say to the man who did not ask you for anything? By God, I will give you what you asked for as long as you ask, even if he does not ask. As for the people of interpretation, they differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: And He gave you everything you desired from Him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told me, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Of everything you asked Him for and desired from Him for it.
Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
Al-Muthanna told me: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, he said: of all that you asked of Him.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He gave you everything you asked for and everything you did not ask for.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Khalaf told us,
m: meaning Ibn Hisham, who said: Mahbub told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Rukanah bin Hashim: From everything you asked Him for, and he said: What you asked Him for and what you did not ask Him for.

x: Others read it as And He gave you from everything you asked Him for, with the tanween of all and leaving out its addition to what, meaning: And He gave you from everything you did not ask Him for or seek from Him. This is because the servants did not ask Him for the sun, the moon, the night, and the day, and He created that for them without them asking Him.
Who said that?
Abu Hasin, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus, told me:

c: Buzay’ told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: regarding this verse: And He gave you of all that you asked Him, he said: What you did not ask Him for.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: that he used to recite: Of everything you asked Him for, and he interpreted it as: He gave you things that you did not ask Him for and did not seek, but I gave them to you through My mercy and generosity. Ad-Dahhak said: How many things has God given us that we did not ask Him for and did not seek?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And He gave you of all that you asked Him for
, meaning: He gave you things that you did not ask for, nor did you ask for them. God is truthful. How many things has God given us that we did not ask Him for, nor did it cross our minds?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He gave you of all that you asked Him for

. He said: You did not ask Him for all that He gave you. Surat Ibrahim 14:34 And He gave you of all you asked of Him. And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is the reading that the reciters of the countries follow, which is adding all to what meaning: And He gave you something of your request, as we have explained before, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it and their rejection of the other reading.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them.

Indeed, mankind is [mostly] unjust and ungrateful.” God the Almighty says: “And if you, O people, should count the favors of God which He has bestowed upon you, you would not be able to enumerate them or give thanks for them except with God’s help for you. “Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful.” He says: The person who exchanges the favor of God for ingratitude is unjust. He says: He is grateful to someone other than the one who bestowed the favor upon him. Thus, by his action, he is putting thanks in the wrong place. This is because God is the One who bestowed the favor upon him, and He deserved that he should sincerely worship Him, so he worshipped someone other than Him and made rivals for Him in order to lead others astray from His path. This is his injustice. And His saying: Ungrateful, He says: He is denying the favor of God that He bestowed upon him by diverting worship to someone other than the one who bestowed the favor upon him, and abandoning the obedience of the one who bestowed the favor upon him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yazid bin Harun told us: Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, who said:
m: The right of God is heavier than the servants can bear, and the blessings of God are more than the servants can count, but they became repentant in the morning and they became repentant in the evening.

evidence.text: Others read it as And He gave you from everything you asked Him for, with the tanween of all and leaving out its addition to what, meaning: And He gave you from everything you did not ask Him for or seek from Him.

The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is the reading that the reciters of the countries follow, which is adding all to what meaning: And He gave you something of your request, as we have explained before, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it and their rejection of the other reading.

x: God Almighty said: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.’

God Almighty says: “And remember, O Muhammad, when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure,’ meaning the sanctuary, a city that is safe for its people and inhabitants, ‘and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.’”

i: It is said of this: “I kept him away from evil, so I keep him away, and I kept him away from evil, so I keep him away, and I kept him away from that, so I keep him away, and from ‘I kept away’ the poet said:
x: And shakes his cradle out of pity for him, and our camels avoid hardships for him.

This means: Keep me and my children away from worshipping idols. Idols are the plural of idol, and an idol is a painted statue, as Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said in describing a woman: Hanana Calzon reveals his idol, laughing at the sweet, veiled Ashnab And Mujahid used to say the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: “And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons from worshipping idols,’” he said: So God answered Abraham’s prayer regarding his children. He said: None of his children worshipped an idol after his return. An idol is a pictured statue. If it is not an idol, then it is a pagan statue. He said: And God answered him, and made this city secure, and provided its people with fruits, and made him an imam, and made from his descendants those who establish prayer, and accepted his prayer, and showed him his rites, and accepted his repentance.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said:
m: Ibrahim al-Taymi used to tell stories and say in his al-Qasas 28:Who is safe from affliction after the friend of God, Ibrahim, when he says: Lord, keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. And His saying: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray. He says: O Lord, indeed the idols have led many people astray. He says: They have led many people astray from the path of guidance and the path of truth until they worshipped them and disbelieved in You.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Indeed, they have led astray many people, meaning the idols.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, they have led astray many people. He said: The idols. And His statement:
h
So whoever follows me

, he is of me, meaning: whoever follows me in what I have of faith in You, sincere worship of You, and abandoning the worship of idols, then he is of me. He means: he follows my Sunnah and acts like I do. And whoever disobeys me, then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: whoever opposes My command and does not accept from Me what I have called him to, and associates others with Him, then indeed You are Forgiving of the sins of the sinners and wrongdoers by Your grace, Merciful to Your servants, You pardon whomever You will among them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever follows me

, he is of me, and whoever disobeys me, - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful. Listen to the words of the friend of God, Abraham. No, by God, they were not slanderers or cursers. It was said: The most evil of God’s servants are every slanderer and curser. The Prophet of God, son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Al-Muthanna narrated: Asbagh bin Al-Faraj narrated:

c: Ibn Wahb told me: Amr bin Al-Harith narrated that Bakr bin Sawada narrated to him on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the words of Abraham: “My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people.
h
So whoever follows me

- indeed, he is of me. And whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.” And Jesus said: If You should punish them - indeed, they are Your servants; but if You forgive them - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. So he raised his hands and said: O God, my nation, O God, my nation, and he wept. So God the Most High said: O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, so ask him what makes him weep? So Gabriel came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him what he had said. He said: So God said: O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say to him: Indeed, We will please you with regard to your nation and will not displease you. Surat Ibrahim 14:36 My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people.
h
So whoever follows me
- then indeed he is of me. And whoever disobeys me - then indeed You are Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

x: And Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, said this statement when he settled Ishmael and his mother Hagar - as mentioned - in Mecca.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Ayoub, who said:
m: I was informed on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first person to walk between Safa and Marwa was the mother of Ismail, and the first thing that the Arab women did, dragging their trains, was the mother of Ismail. He said: When she fled from Sarah, she let down her train to cover her tracks, so Ibrahim came with her and Ismail until he reached the place of the House, and he put them down and then returned, so she followed him and said: What are you leaving us to? Are you leaving us to food? Are you leaving us to drink? He did not answer her anything, so she said: Did God command you to do this? He said: Yes, she said: Then He will not let us down. He said: So I returned and he continued until he had reached the top of his mountain pass, then he turned towards the valley and supplicated, saying: “Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they may be grateful.” He said: And with the woman was a sack of water, but the water ran out and she became thirsty, and her milk stopped, so the child became thirsty. So she looked to which of the mountains was lowest to the earth, so she ascended Safa and listened to see if she could hear a sound or see a companion. She did not hear, so she descended. When she came to the valley, she ran, but she did not intend to run, like a tired person who runs, but does not intend to run. She looked at which mountains were lower than the ground, so she climbed up Al-Marwah and listened to see if she could hear a sound or see a companion. She heard a sound, so she said, like a person who denies his hearing: Hush! until she was filled with water. She said: You have made me hear your voice, so help me, for I have perished and those with me have perished. Then the angel came and brought her until her master reached the place of Zamzam. He struck it with his foot, and a spring gushed forth. The woman hurried and put it in her bag. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on the mother of Ismail. Had she not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” The king said to her: Do not fear thirst for the people of this country, for it is a spring for the drinking of God’s guests. He said: The father of this boy will come and they will build a house for God in this place. He said: A group of Jurhum passed by, intending to go to Syria, and they saw the bird on the mountain, and they said: This bird is craving water. Do you know what water is in this valley? They said: No. So they looked out and saw the woman, so they went to her and asked her to come down with them, and she gave them permission. He said: And what befalls these people of death befell her, so she died, and Ishmael married a woman from them. Then Abraham came and asked about Ishmael's house until he was directed to it, but he did not find it. He found a woman of his who was rough and coarse, so he said to her: When your husband comes, tell him: An old man of such and such description has come here, and he says to you: I am not satisfied with the threshold of your door for you, so move it and go. When Ishmael came, she told him, so he said: That is my father and you are the grape of my door. So he divorced her and married another woman from them. Abraham came until he reached Ishmael's house, but he did not find it, and he found a woman of his who was easy and free, so he said to her: Where did your husband go? She said: He went hunting. He said: What is your food? She said: Meat and water. He said: O God, bless their meat and water for them. O God, bless their meat and water for them three times. Then he said to her: When your husband comes, tell him. Say: An old man of such and such description has come here, and he says to you: I have approved the threshold of your door for you, so make it firm. Then when Ishmael came, she told him. He said: Then he came a third time, and they raised the foundations of the House. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated: Yahya bin Ibad narrated: Hammad bin Salamah narrated: Ata bin Al-Saib narrated: Saeed bin Jubair narrated: Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet of God, Abraham, came with Ishmael and Hagar and put them in Mecca at the place of Zamzam. When he had gone, Hagar called out to him: O Abraham, I only ask you three times: Who ordered you to put me in a land where there is no udder, no crops, no companions, no provisions, and no water? He said: My Lord ordered me. She said: He will never let us down. When Abraham turned back, he said: Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare, meaning from grief. And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven, meaning from grief. When Ishmael was thirsty, he began to push the ground with his heel. Hagar went until she climbed Safa, and the valley at that time was deep, so she climbed Safa and looked out to see if she could see anything. She did not see anything, so she descended and reached the valley, and walked in it until she came out of it, then she came to Al-Marwah, and climbed up and looked to see if she could see anything, but she did not see anything. She did that seven times, then she came from Al-Marwah to Ismail, and he was pushing the ground with his heel, and the spring had sprung forth, which was Zamzam. She began to examine the ground with her hand for water, and whenever water gathered, she would take it in her cup and pour it into her waterskin. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on her. If she had left it, it would have been a flowing spring that would run until the Day of Resurrection.” He said: At that time, Jurhum was in a valley near Mecca. He said: The birds stayed in the valley when they saw water. When Jurhum saw the birds, they stayed in the valley. They said: You only stayed in it if there was water in it. So they came to Hagar and said: If you wish, we will be with you and provide you with comfort, and the water is your water. She said: Yes. So they stayed with her until Ishmael grew up, and Hagar died, and Ishmael married a woman from them. He said: Abraham asked Sarah for permission to go to Hagar, and she gave him permission and stipulated that he not go down. Abraham came and Hagar had died, so he went to Ishmael’s house and said to his wife: Where is your companion? She said: He is not here. He went hunting. Ishmael used to go out from the sanctuary to hunt and then return. Abraham said: Do you have hospitality? Do you have food or drink? She said: I do not have it, and no one is with me. Abraham said: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him to change the threshold of his door. Abraham went, and Ishmael came and smelled the scent of his father. He said to his wife: Has anyone come to you? She said: An old man came to me, as if he was making light of his situation. He said: What did he say to you? She said: He said to me: Greet your husband and tell him to change the threshold of his door. So he divorced her and married another. Abraham stayed as long as God willed him to stay. Then he asked Sarah for permission to visit Ishmael, and she gave him permission, but stipulated that he should not come down. Abraham came until he reached Ishmael's door and said to his wife: Where is your companion? She said: He went hunting, and he will come back now, God willing. Come down, may God have mercy on you. He said to her: Do you have something to offer? She said: Yes. He said: Do you have bread, wheat, dates, or barley? She said: No. So she brought milk and meat, and he invoked blessings for them. If she had brought bread, wheat, barley or dates that day, it would have been the land of God with the most wheat, barley and dates. She said to him: Come down so I can wash your head, but he did not come down. So she brought him the Maqam and placed it on his right side, and he put his foot on it, and the mark of his foot remained on it. So she washed the right side of his head, then she moved the Maqam to his left side and washed his left side. Then he said to her: When your husband comes, greet him with my greetings and say to him: The threshold of your door has been made straight. When Ishmael came, he smelled the scent of his father, so he said to his wife: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, an old man with the most handsome face and the best scent. He said to me such and such, and I said to him such and such, and I washed his head, and this is the place where his foot was on the Maqam. He said: What did he say to you? She said: He said to me: When your husband comes, greet him with my greetings and say to him: The threshold of your door has been made straight. He said: That was Ibrahim. So he stayed as long as God willed him to stay, and God commanded him to build the House, so he and Ishmael built it. When they had built it, it was said: Proclaim the Hajj to the people. So he did not pass by a people except that he said: O people, a House has been built for you, so perform Hajj to it. But no one heard him, neither rock nor tree nor anything else, except that he said: Here I am, O God, here I am. He said: And between his saying: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, and his saying: Praise be to God, who has given me in my old age Ishmael and Isaac, there were so many years. Ata’ did not memorize it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, and it is a house that God has purified from evil, and made it a qiblah, and made it His sanctuary, and the Prophet of God, Abraham, chose it for his son.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Without crops. He said: There was no crops in Mecca at that time.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Kathir informed me, Al-Qasim said
m: in his hadith: He said: Amr ibn Kathir informed me.

x: So I changed it and made it: He said:

c: Ibn Kathir informed me,
m: and I omitted Amr, because I do not know a person called Amr ibn Kathir from whom Ibn Jurayj narrated. Muʿmar narrated it from Kathir ibn Kathir ibn Al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wadaʿah, and I fear that the hadith of Ibn Jurayj is also from Kathir ibn Kathir, he said: I and Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman were with some people with Saʿid ibn Jubayr at night, so Saʿid ibn Jubayr said to the al-Nas 114:Ask me before you ask me, so the people asked him a lot, and among what he was asked about was that he was asked: Is what we heard in the place true? So Saʿid said: What did you hear? They said: We heard that when Abraham, the Messenger of God, came from Ash-Sham, he swore to his wife that he would not go down to Mecca until he returned, so the place of standing was brought near to him, and he went down to it. Saeed said: It is not like what Ibn Abbas told us, but he told us when he was between the mother of Surat Ibrahim 14:37 Our Lord, indeed I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So fill hearts among the people with inclination toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they may be grateful. Ismail and Sarah, and he did not come with Ismail. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ayoub, except that he added to his hadith, he said: Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said before: And for this reason the people circumambulated between Safa and Marwa, then he narrated and said: Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They asked to go down with her, and the mother of Ismail loved companionship, so they went down and sent to their family, so they came, and their food was game, they would go out from the sanctuary and Ismail would go out with them to hunt, and when he reached puberty they married him, and his mother had died before that. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When he prayed for them that their meat and water would be blessed, he said to her: Is there grain or other food? She said: No, and if he had found grain for her that day, he would have prayed for her to be blessed in it.” Ibn Abbas said: Then he stayed as long as God willed him to stay, then he came and found Ismail sitting under a tree on the side of the well sharpening his arrows, so he greeted him and went down to him, and sat with him and said: O Ismail, God has commanded me to do something, Ismail said: So obey your Lord in what He commanded you, Abraham said: He commanded me to build a house for Him, Ismail said: Build, Ibn Abbas said: Abraham pointed to a hill in front of him, high above what was around it, and the flood came to it from its sides but did not cover it. He said: So they got up digging from the foundations, raising them and saying: Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearer, the Knower, Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearer of supplication, and Ismail carried the stones on his neck, and the old man Ibrahim was building, and when the building rose and it was difficult for the old man to reach it, Ismail brought this stone to him, and he began to stand on it and build, and move it around the sides of the House until he finished, Ibn Abbas said: So that was the standing place of Abraham and his standing on it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley. He said: Ishmael and his mother settled in Mecca.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: I settled some of my descendants in a valley without crops. He said: When Ishmael was born.

x: The interpretation of the statement then is: Our Lord, I have settled some of my children in a valley without crops. And in his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is evidence that there was no water there that day, because if there had been water there, he would not have described it as being without crops near your house, which you have forbidden all of your creation to make permissible.
And his prohibition of it was mentioned as follows:

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab said in his sermon: The first to take charge of this House were people from Tasm, so they disobeyed their Lord, violated His sanctity, and belittled His right, so God destroyed them. Then people from Jurhum took charge of it, so they disobeyed their Lord, violated His sanctity, and belittled His right, so God destroyed them. Then you took charge of it, O people of Quraysh. So do not disobey its Lord, do not violate His sanctity, and do not belittle His right. By God, one prayer in it is more beloved to me than a hundred prayers elsewhere. And know that sins in it are of a similar nature. He said, I settled some of my descendants in a valley without crops, and he did not mention what the action was based on, because the point of speech is to say, I settled some of my descendants, or a man, or a people, and that is not permissible with min, because it indicates what is meant by the speech, and the Arabs do that with it a lot, so they say, We killed some of the Banu so-and-so, “We ate from the grass,” and We drank from the water. From this is the saying of God Almighty, Pour upon us some water or from what God has provided you.

x: How did Abraham say when he settled his son in Mecca, Indeed, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, and it was narrated in the reports that you mentioned that Abraham built the House after that for a period of time?

There have been statements made about that that I mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, including that its meaning is: near Your sacred House that was before You raised it from the earth when You raised it during the days of the flood. And among them is near Your sacred House that had previously been known to you to occur in this country. And his saying: the sacred, according to what Qatada said, its meaning is: the sacred of making permissible the sacred things of God in it, and belittling His right. And his saying, Our Lord, that they may establish prayer, he says: You did that, O our Lord, so that Your obligatory prayers that You made obligatory upon them may be performed in Your sacred House. And His saying:
h
So make the hearts of some people yearn toward them

, God Almighty informs us of this about His friend Abraham, that he asked Him in his supplication to make the hearts of some of His creation yearn toward the dwellings of his descendants whom He settled in an uncultivated valley near His sacred House, and that was a supplication from Him for them that He would grant them the opportunity to perform the Hajj to His sacred House.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: The hearts of the people yearn for them. If he had said: The hearts of the people yearn for them, the Jews, Christians, and Magians would have been an argument, but he said: The hearts of the people yearn for them, and they are the Muslims.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So make the hearts of the people yearn for them. He said: If it were the hearts of the people, the Persians and the Romans would have crowded around him, but it is the hearts of the people.

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then make the hearts of the people yearn for them. He said: If he had said the hearts of the people yearn for them, the Persians and the Romans would have crowded around them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ali told us,
m: meaning Ibn Al-Ja’d, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said:
m: I asked Ikrimah about this verse: Then make the hearts of the people incline toward them. He said: Their hearts incline toward the House.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: Ata’, and Tawus:
h
So make the hearts of the people yearn toward them
. The verse: Their hearts yearn toward it, they come to it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, who said:
m: I asked Ata’, Tawus, and Ikrimah about His statement:
h
So make the hearts of the people yearn toward them
. They said: Hajj.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Shababah and Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, they said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ata’,
m: Tawus, and Ikrimah, regarding his statement:
h
So make the hearts of the people incline toward them
, he said: Their inclination toward Mecca is to perform Hajj.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Adam told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: I asked Tawus, Ikrimah, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, about his statement:
h
So make the hearts of the people incline toward them
, and they said: Make their inclination the Hajj.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If Abraham had said: Then make the hearts of the people incline toward them, it would have been an argument for the Jews, the Christians, and all the people. But he said: The hearts of the people incline toward them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then make the hearts of some people incline toward them
, he said: incline toward them.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

x: Others said: He only prayed for them to live in Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then make hearts among the people yearn toward them
, he said: Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, asked God to make some people yearn to live in or reside in Mecca. And His statement:
h
And provide them with fruits
, God Almighty says:
h
And provide them with fruits

of plants and trees as You provide for the inhabitants of the countryside and villages that have water and rivers, even if You had settled them in a valley without crops or water, then He, the Most High, would have provided them with that.

c: Al-Muthanna also told me: Ishaq told us: Hisham told us:
m: I read to Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta’ifi that when Abraham prayed for the sanctuary, And provide its people with fruits, God moved Al-Ta’if from Palestine. And His saying: Perhaps they will be grateful, means: So that they may thank You for what You have provided for them and bestowed upon them.

x: This is report from God Almighty about His friend Abraham’s martyrdom of him for what he intended and meant by his supplication and saying, My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons from worshipping idols .... the verse, and that he only intended by that to please God with him in his love for his son to be among the people of obedience to God, and to sincerely worship Him in the same way that he is for Him, so he said: Our Lord, You know what our hearts conceal when we ask You for what we ask, and in other conditions of ours, and what we declare of our supplication, so we proclaim it and other than that of our deeds, and nothing is hidden from You, O our Lord, of anything that is on earth or in heaven, because all of that is apparent to You, manifest and evident, because You are its Manager and Creator, so how could it be hidden from You.

He says: Praise be to God who has given me, in my old age, sons Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication. He says: Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of my supplication that I call upon Him with, and my saying: Make this city secure and keep me and my children from worshipping idols, and other than that of my supplication and the supplication of others, and everything that is spoken by a speaker from whom nothing is hidden.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar bin Marra, who said:
m: I heard an old man telling Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Abraham was given good report after one hundred and seventeen years.

x: He says: O Lord, make me one who performs what You have obligated me to do of Your obligation which You have imposed upon me of prayer. And from my offspring. He says: And also make from my offspring those who establish prayer for You. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. He says: Our Lord, and accept my work which I do for You, and my worship of You. This is similar to the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Indeed, supplication is worship.
“And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.”
This is a supplication from Abraham, may God’s prayers be upon him, for his parents to be forgiven, and a request for forgiveness from him for them.

c: God Almighty has informed us that
m: (Abraham’s request for forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing.) We have already explained the time of his acquittal, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. His statement:
h
And for the believers
means: And for those who believe in you from among those who follow me in the religion that I am upon, and obey you in your commands and prohibitions. His statement:
h
On the Day when the reckoning takes place
means: People will stand for the reckoning, so He was satisfied with mentioning the reckoning instead of mentioning the people, since its meaning was understood.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not think, O Muhammad, that God is unaware of what these polytheists among your people do. Rather, He knows them and their deeds, and He keeps them accountable, so that He may reward them with their reward at the time that He has already known that He will reward them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ali bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Burqan, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do
, he said: It is a warning to the wrongdoer and consolation to the wronged.

x: God Almighty says: He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare in horror.

God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, only delays these wrongdoers who deny you and reject your prophethood until a day when eyes will stare in horror. He says: He only delays their punishment and the infliction of torment upon them until a day when the eyes of creation will stare in horror, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: On a Day when eyes will stare in horror, by God, their eyes will stare in horror, and they will not return to them. As for his saying: rushing, the people of interpretation differed about its meaning.

x: Some of them said: its meaning is: hastening.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Mu’addab, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Rushing, he said: The trotting, which is the trot, or less than the trot, doubt or Saeed, they trot while they watch.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Rushing, he said: Hastening.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Rushing, he says: setting out, intending to go to the caller.

x: Others said: It means: long-sighted.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: looking without blinking, meaning by looking without blinking.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Masrouq, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha,
m: Muhta’een, he said: Ihta’ is the constant, unblinking blush.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abu al-Khair bin Tamim bin Hudlam, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement: rushing, he said: rushing is to rush.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Muhta’een means intense staring without blinking.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: rushing, he said: intense staring without blinking.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: staring intently, staring is: looking intently without blinking.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Muhta’in he said:
m: Long-sighted.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: He does not raise his head.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Muhta’in, he said: The one who does not raise his head. And Ihta’a in the speech of the Arabs means to hasten, more famous than it means to keep looking, and from Ihta’a in the meaning of hastening, is the saying of the poet: And in a clearing, as if its reins were on the top of a pruned Awal trunk. And the other said: I can send messengers as if his braid is a reckless one from a fasting person who is forbidden His saying: with their heads covered, means with their heads raised. Covering the head means raising it. From this comes the saying of Al-Shamakh: They attack the bitches with their molars covered like a falling camel. Meaning: They come early to the tamarisk tree with their heads raised up to it so that it can take some of it. From this also comes the saying of the rajaz poet: He lowered his head towards me and looked at me as if he had seen something greedy. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: with their heads covered, he said: Covering means raising their heads.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told me, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: and Al-Hasan said, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: with their heads covered, he said: raising them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Saad, who said: Al-Hasan said:
m: People’s faces on the Day of Resurrection will be towards the sky, and no one will look at anyone else.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Suwaid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad,
m: that he heard Mujahid say regarding His statement: rushing with their heads bowed down, he said: raising his head like this, not turning their glance back to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: with their heads covered, he said: with their heads raised.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: With their heads covered, he said: covering means raising their heads.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Those with their heads covered, he said: The one who covers his head is the one who raises his head, staring, not blinking.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: with their heads covered, he said: raising them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: with their heads covered, he said: The one who covers his head is the one who raises his head.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: With their heads covered, he said: With their heads raised.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: With their heads covered, he said: With their heads raised. His saying:
h
Their glances will not return to them
, means: Their eyes will not return to them because of the intensity of their gaze.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their glances will not return to them
, and their hearts will be empty, he said: Their eyes will be fixed. His saying:
h
And their hearts are empty
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: torn apart and does not comprehend anything good.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: They are torn apart and do not comprehend anything.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Malik ibn Mughul told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told us: Sahl bin Amer told us: Malik and Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra:
m: h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: They are torn apart and do not comprehend anything good.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us:
m: Malik, meaning Ibn Mughul, told us: I heard Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, except that he said: Do not understand anything, and he did not say good.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Malik bin Mughul and Israel told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra,
m: h
And their hearts are empty
, one of them said: ruined, and the other said: torn apart and not understanding anything.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: There is nothing good in them, so they are like ruins.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: There is nothing good in their hearts, like you saying about a house in which there is nothing, it is only air.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And their hearts are empty

, he said: The hearts are empty, as God said, Surat Ibrahim 14:43 Rushing forward, their heads covered, their glances not turning back to them, and their hearts empty of air. there is no mind or benefit in them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Bakra, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: There is nothing good in them.

x: Others said: It does not settle in a place that is repeated in their stomachs.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And their hearts are empty
space, he said: They are raging in their stomachs, with no place to settle in.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that it came out of its place and stuck in the throat.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha:
m: h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: It has reached their throats.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their hearts are empty
, he said: Empty, with nothing in it, it came out of their chests and stuck in their throats.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: And their hearts are air, was taken away until it was in their throats, not leaving their mouths, nor returning to its place. The first of these sayings, in my opinion, that is the most correct in interpreting that is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: It is empty, there is nothing good in it, and it does not comprehend anything. This is because the Arabs call everything hollow and empty: air. From this is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit: Tell Abu Sufyan about me, you are hollow and empty And from it the other said: Do not be among those who are taken by every bird of prey, like the spring of milk, whose heart is broken.

x: God Almighty says: And warn, O Muhammad, the people to whom I have sent you as a caller to Islam, of what will befall them on the Day when God’s punishment comes to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Then those who did wrong will say, meaning those who disbelieved in their Lord, and thereby wronged themselves, Our Lord, delay us, meaning delay Your punishment from us, and give us respite for a short term, so that we may answer Your call, the truth, so that we may believe in You and not associate anything with You, and follow the messengers, meaning that we believe in Your messengers, so that we may follow them in what You have called us to of obeying You and following Your command. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement:
h
And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them
, he said: the Day of Resurrection. Then those who did wrong will say, ‘Our Lord, delay us for a short term,’ he said: a period in which they will work in this world.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them
, meaning: warn them in this world before the punishment comes to them. His saying: And those who did wrong will say is in the nominative case in apposition to his saying:
h
The punishment will come to them
, in his saying:
h
The punishment will come to them
, and it is not an answer to the command. If it were an answer to his saying:
h
And warn the people

, then the nominative and accusative cases would be permissible for it. As for the accusative case, it is as the poet said: Oh camel, go with a broad neck to Solomon, so that we may rest. And the nominative is for resumption. It was mentioned about Al-Ala’ bin Sayyaba that he used to reject the accusative in response to the command with the letter fa’. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Ala’ was the one who taught Muadh and his companions.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Did you not swear before that you would not perish?

This is a rebuke from God Almighty to the polytheists of Quraysh, after they entered the Fire for denying in this world the resurrection after death. He says to them when they asked Him to lift the punishment from them, and to delay them so that they might repent and turn back: Did you not swear before that you would not perish? He says: You will not have a transition from this world to the Hereafter, and you will only die and then not be resurrected.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Did you not swear before, like his statement: (And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that God would not resurrect anyone who dies. Yes.) Then he said: You will not have any passing away. He said: The transition from this world to the hereafter.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Salamah told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: There is no disappearance for you, he said: You will not die, referring to the Quraysh.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Laila,
m: one of the Banu Amir, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say: Or was it mentioned to me that the people of Hell will call out, Our Lord, delay us for a short term, so that we may answer Your call and follow the messengers. He replied to them, Did you not swear before that you would not perish? And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves.... until His saying, so that the mountains may move from it.

x: God the Almighty says: And you dwelt in this world in the dwellings of those who disbelieved in God, and wronged themselves thereby from the nations that were before you, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them. He says: And you knew how We destroyed them when they rebelled against their Lord, and persisted in their transgression and disbelief. And We presented to you examples. He says: And We presented to you examples of what you were upon of associating partners with God, establishing examples, but you did not repent or turn from your disbelief, so now you ask for a delay for repentance when what has befallen you of punishment has befallen you, that will not happen. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves

, he said: The people dwelt in the dwellings of the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, and many generations between them from among the nations who perished. And it will become clear to you how We dealt with them, and We presented to you examples, by God, He sent His messengers and revealed His books, and presented to you examples, so none but the deaf are deaf in them, and none but the disappointed are disappointed in them, so understand God’s command.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves

, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, he said: They dwelt in their villages, Madyan and Al-Hijr, and the villages whose people God punished, and it became clear to you how God dealt with them, and He gave them examples.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement: The parables he said: The similarities.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: God Almighty says: Those who wronged themselves plotted, so you lived after them in their dwellings, their plot.
And their plot that they plotted was what:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya told me: Sufyan told us: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abaan:
m: I heard Ali reciting:
h
And if their plot were to move mountains from it

, he said: A king took young eagles and fed them meat until they grew up, became strong and thick. Then he and his companion sat in the coffin and tied the coffin to the legs of the eagles and hung the meat above the coffin. Every time they looked at the meat, they climbed up and up. Then he said to his companion: What do you see? He said: I see mountains like smoke. He said: What do you see? He said: I see nothing. He said: Woe to you, you are on the right track. He said: “That is what His statement: “
h
And if their plot were to move mountains from it

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Wasil, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib,
m: like the hadith of Yahya bin Saʿid, and he added to it: And Abdullah bin Masʿud used to recite it, even though their plot was such that mountains would move from it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated: Muhammad bin Abi Uday narrated on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: Abd al-Rahman bin Wasil narrated that Ali said about this verse:
h
And if their plot

were to remove mountains from it, he said: The one who argued with Abraham about his Lord took two small eagles and brought them close, then they grew thick and strong and became young men. He said: So a man tied each one of them to a coffin with a peg and starved them, and he and another man sat in the coffin. He said: And he raised a stick in the coffin with meat on his head. He said: So they flew away, and he kept saying to his companion: Look what you see? He said: I see such and such, until he said: I see the world as if it were a fly. So he said: Point the stick, so he pointed it and they both fell. He said: So this is the saying of God the Most High:
h
And if their plot
were to remove mountains from it. Abu Ishaq said: And it is the same in the recitation of Abdullah:
h
And if their plot
were to remove mountains from it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Even though their plot was to move mountains, it was the plot of Persia. He claimed that Nebuchadnezzar came out with eagles, and made a coffin for himself to enter, and he placed spears at its ends and the flesh above them. I think he said: It did so, going toward the flesh until his sight was cut off from the land and its people, and it was called: O tyrant, where are you going? So he was frightened, then he heard a voice above him, so he aimed the spears, and the eagles aimed, and the mountains were startled by their shaking, and the mountains almost moved from it from the sound of that, so that is what he said: Even though their plot was to move mountains.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said:
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: They plotted their plot, and with God is their plot, and their plot was almost like this. Mujahid read it, their plot was almost like this, so the mountains were removed from it. He said: Some of those who passed away starved eagles, then he placed a coffin over them and entered it, then he placed spears with flesh at the ends of them, so they began to see the flesh, and they would go, until his sight ended, and it was called: O tyrant, where are you going? So he aimed the spears, and the eagles aimed, and the mountains were startled, and they thought that the Hour had come, so they were almost removed. So that is what God the Most High said: And their plot was almost like this, so the mountains were removed from it. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he used to recite: And their plot almost made the mountains move. This hadith was told to me by Ahmad bin Yusuf. He said: Al-Qasim bin Salam told us. He said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to recite it in the manner of litazul with the first lam open and the second lam raised.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Danil, who said:
m: I heard Ali say: Even if their plot is such that mountains move. Surat Ibrahim 14:46 And they planned their plan, but with God is their plan, even though their plan was such that mountains would move.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Daneel, who said:
m: I heard Ali say:
h
And if their plot

were to move mountains, he said: Then Ali began to narrate and said: It was revealed about a tyrant among the tyrants. He said: I will not stop until I know what is in the heavens. Then he took eagles and began to feed them meat until they grew thick and strong and became powerful, and he mentioned a hadith similar to Shu’bah’s. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Abu Dawud Al-Hadrami narrated on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Hafs bin Hameed or Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
h
And if their plot

was to make mountains move, he said: Nimrod, the master of the eagles, ordered a coffin to be made and he placed a man with it, then he ordered the eagles to be carried. When he ascended, he said to his companion: What do you see? He said: I see water and an island, meaning the world. Then he ascended and said to his companion: What do you see? He said: We only grow further away from the sky. He said: Descend. Another one said: It was called, O tyrant, where are you going? He said: So the mountains heard the rustling of the eagles, and they thought it was more powerful than the sky, so they almost moved. This is what He said:
h
And if their plot
was to make mountains move.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas,
m: that Anas used to recite: And their plot was such that mountains would move from it.

x: Others said: Their plot was their associating partners with God and their slander against Him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And their plot was such that the mountains would move. He said: Their polytheism is like His saying:
h
The heavens almost burst from it

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And their plot was such that the mountains would move. He said: It is like His statement: And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son.’ You have certainly done a thing at which the heavens almost burst and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if their plot
was, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that Al-Hasan used to say: He was too insignificant to God and too small for the mountains to move from him, describing them with that. Qatada said: In the copy of the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Masoud it is: And their plot almost made the mountains move from him, and Qatada used to say at that time:
h
The heavens almost burst from it
, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation. That is, because of their speech.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if their plot were to cause the mountains to move
, he said that when they attributed a son to God. And he said in another verse:
h
The heavens almost burst from it
, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And their plot was such that the mountains would move away in the wording of Ibn Masʿud
: And their plot was such that the mountains would move away is like His statement:
h
The heavens almost burst from it

, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: that the mountains might move from it. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madinah, and Iraq read it, except for Al-Kisa'i,
h
And if their plot
was to remove the mountains from it, with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: And their plot was not to remove the mountains from it. Al-Kisa'i read it,
h
And if their plot
was to remove the mountains from it, with a fatha on the first lam and a nominative on the second, based on the interpretation of the reading of those who read it,
h
And if their plot

was to remove the mountains from it, from the earlier scholars whose statements were mentioned, meaning: Their plot became intense until the mountains moved from it, or almost moved from it. Al-Kisa'i used to narrate on the authority of Hamza, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to read it in the same way as his reading,
h
And if their plot
was to remove the mountains from it, with a nominative on the letter tazul.

c: Al-Harith told me
m: this on the authority of Al-Qasim on his authority. The correct reading, according to us, is the reading of those who read it as
h
and if their plot

was such that mountains would move from it with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: and their plot was not such that mountains would move from it. We said: This is correct, because if the first lam is opened, the meaning of the statement is: And their plot was such that the mountains would move, and if they had moved they would not have remained, and in its remaining in its state there is what shows that it did not move, and another is the consensus of the proof from the reciters on that, and in that there is sufficient evidence for its correctness, and the corruption of others by something else.

x: If someone thinks that this is not a consensus of the proof, since there were some of the Companions and Followers who read it like this, then the matter is contrary to what he thought about that, and that is that those who read it with the opening of the first lam and the raising of the second read wa-wa-kad makrahum with the dal, and if it is read like this, then the correct reading with wa-wa-kad is to open the first lam and raise the second according to what they read, and it is not permissible for us to read like this, because our Qur’ans are different from that, and the script of our Qur’ans is with the nun and not the dal, and since it is like this, then it is not permissible for anyone to change the script of the Qur’ans of the Muslims, and if that is not permissible then the correct reading is only what the readers of the regions are upon, not those who deviate in their reading from them.
And similar to what we said about the meaning of even if their plot was, a group of interpreters said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: And they plotted their plot, but with God is their plot, even though their plot was such that mountains would move. He said: Their plot was not such that mountains would move.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said:
m: Al-Hasan said, regarding His statement:
h
And if their plot was to move mountains
, their plot was not to move mountains.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: Their plot was not such that mountains would move.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Yunus and Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And their plot was such that mountains would move. They said: Al-Hasan used to say: And their plot was so weak and feeble that mountains would move. He said: Harun said: Yunus informed me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: There are four things in the Qur’an:
h
And if their plot

was such that mountains would move from it: Their plot was such that mountains would not move from it. His statement: We would have taken him from Our presence, if We were to do so: We would not do so. His statement: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers: The Most Gracious had no son. His statement: And We have certainly empowered them in that in which We have empowered you: We have empowered you in that in which We have empowered you. Harun said: Amr bin Asbat narrated them to me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and he added one more to them: If you are in doubt: I am not in doubt about what We have revealed to you. The first is to say that it is correct in interpreting the verse, since the reading that was mentioned is correct, based on what we have explained of the evidence in His statement: And they have plotted their plot, but with God is their plot, even though their plot was such that mountains would move. Those who wronged themselves associated others with their Lord, and they fabricated a lie against Him, but with God is knowledge of their association with Him and their fabrication against Him, and He will punish them for that with the punishment that they deserve. Their association and their slander against God was not such that mountains would move, but rather they harmed none thereby except themselves, and their hateful intention did not return except against them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shammar, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: Treachery is deceit, and deceit is disbelief.

evidence.text: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Wasil, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, like the hadith of Yahya bin Saʿid, and he added to it: And Abdullah bin Masʿud used to recite it, even though their plot was such that mountains would move from it.
Abu Ishaq said: And it is the same in the recitation of Abdullah: And if their plot were to remove mountains from it.
Mujahid read it, their plot was almost like this, so the mountains were removed from it.
He said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to recite it in the manner of litazul with the first lam open and the second lam raised.
The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: that the mountains might move from it.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madinah, and Iraq read it, except for Al-Kisa'i, And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it, with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: And their plot was not to remove the mountains from it.

Al-Kisa'i read it, And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it, with a fatha on the first lam and a nominative on the second, based on the interpretation of the reading of those who read it, And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it, from the earlier scholars whose statements were mentioned, meaning: Their plot became intense until the mountains moved from it, or almost moved from it.

Al-Kisa'i used to narrate on the authority of Hamza, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to read it in the same way as his reading, And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it, with a nominative on the letter tazul.

The correct reading, according to us, is the reading of those who read it as and if their plot was such that mountains would move from it with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: and their plot was not such that mountains would move from it.

We said: This is correct, because if the first lam is opened, the meaning of the statement is: And their plot was such that the mountains would move, and if they had moved they would not have remained, and in its remaining in its state there is what shows that it did not move, and another is the consensus of the proof from the reciters on that, and in that there is sufficient evidence for its correctness, and the corruption of others by something else.

If someone thinks that this is not a consensus of the proof, since there were some of the Companions and Followers who read it like this, then the matter is contrary to what he thought about that, and that is that those who read it with the opening of the first lam and the raising of the second read wa-wa-kad makrahum with the dal, and if it is read like this, then the correct reading with wa-wa-kad is to open the first lam and raise the second according to what they read, and it is not permissible for us to read like this, because our Qur’ans are different from that, and the script of our Qur’ans is with the nun and not the dal, and since it is like this, then it is not permissible for anyone to change the script of the Qur’ans of the Muslims, and if that is not permissible then the correct reading is only what the readers of the regions are upon, not those who deviate in their reading from them.

The first is to say that it is correct in interpreting the verse, since the reading that was mentioned is correct, based on what we have explained of the evidence in His statement: And they have plotted their plot, but with God is their plot, even though their plot was such that mountains would move.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So do not think that God will fail in His promise, which He promised them when they lied and denied what they brought to them from Him. God Almighty only said this to His Prophet to strengthen and reinforce his resolve, and to know that He sent down His wrath upon those who lied to Him and denied His prophethood, and rejected what He brought to them from God, an example of what He sent down upon those who followed their path from the nations who were before them on the same path of denying their messengers, denying their prophethood, and rejecting what they brought to them from God upon them. His saying: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution, means by his saying Indeed, God is Exalted in Might: Nothing that He wants to punish can prevent Him. He is able to do anything to anyone who seeks Him.

He does not escape Him by fleeing from Him. The One who takes revenge from those who disbelieved in His Messengers and denied them, and denied their prophethood, and associated partners with Him and took with Him a god other than Him. His saying,
h
Mukhalaf was added to the promise
, and it is a source, because it occurred in the position of a noun, and His saying,
h
His messengers was made accusative by

meaning, and that is because the meaning is: Do not think that God will fail His messengers in His promise. So the promiser, even if it is lowered by adding Mukhalaf to it, is in the meaning of the accusative, and that is because the failure is done on two different accusatives, like the saying of the one who says: I clothed Abdullah with a garment, and brought him into a house. And if the verb is like that, it is done on two different accusatives, and it is permissible to bring forward whichever one is brought forward, and lower what follows the verb that is in the form of nouns, and lower the second, so it is said: I am the entrance of Abdullah into the house, and I am the entrance of Abdullah, if you bring the house forward to the entrance and delay Abdullah, you lower the house, because the entrance was added to it, and Abdullah is accusative, and if Abdullah is brought forward to it, and the house is delayed, Abdullah is lowered by adding the entrance to it, and the house is accusative, and it did that like that, because the verb, I mean the entrance, works in every One of them is an accusative case for its action in the other, and from this is the poet’s saying: You see the bull in it, its head and the rest of it are exposed to the sun.

He added an entrance to the shadow, and erected the head, but the meaning of the speech is: the entrance of his head is the shadow. And from it is the saying of another: Brush me with goodness, lest I be, and praise me as a rock moaning on a day of honey. Al-Usayl: the feather used to collect perfume. The meaning of the statement is: like a rock that was mowed one day with a feather. And likewise the saying of another: My cousin Salma is a cook who cooks during the hours of sleep, and laziness increases. The meaning of the words is: A cook who provides the laziness during the hours of sleep. As for the one who reads this, do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers. We have already explained the reason for its being correct in the speech of the Arabs in Surat Al-An’am, when He said And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

evidence.text: As for the one who reads this, do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers.

x: God Almighty says: God is the possessor of vengeance
h
on the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens as well against the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, from Quraysh, and all those who disbelieved in God and denied your prophethood and the prophethood of His messengers before you. So it is a day of vengeance. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced with another earth
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: On the Day the earth that people are on today in this world will be replaced with another earth, and it will become a white earth like silver.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: I heard ʿAmr ibn Maymun narrating, on the authority of ʿAbdullah, that he said regarding this verse:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well], he said: An earth like pure silver, in which no blood has been shed, and in which no sin has been committed. They will hear the caller, and their sight will penetrate them, barefoot and naked, standing. I think he said: As they were created, until sweat bridles them standing alone. Shuʿbah said: Then I heard him say: I heard Amr bin Maymun, and he did not mention Abdullah. Then I repeated it to him, and he said:
Hubayrah told me, on the authority of Abdullah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us: Shu’bah told us: Abu Ishaq told us:
