m: I heard Amr bin Maymun - and perhaps he said: Abdullah said: and perhaps he did not say, so I said to him: On the authority of Abdullah, he said: I heard Amr bin Maymun - say: On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth. He said: An earth like silver, white and pure, in which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed in it. Their sight will penetrate and they will hear the caller, barefoot and naked as they were created. He said: I think he said: Standing until sweat bridles them.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Shababah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, and the heavens [as well], he said: It will be replaced by a white, pure earth as if it were silver, in which no forbidden blood has been shed, and in which no sin has been committed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, he said: The earth of Paradise will be white and pure, no sin will be committed in it, they will hear the caller, their sight will penetrate, they will be barefoot and naked standing, bridled by sweat.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun,
m: h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: A white earth like silver in which no forbidden blood has been shed, and no sin has been committed in it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us: Hammad bin Zaid told us: Asim bin Bahdalah told us, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud,
m: that he recited this verse:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well], and they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing. He said: A white earth will be brought, as if it were a silver ingot, in which no blood has been shed, and no sin has been committed upon it. He said: So the first thing that will be judged between the people will be regarding blood. Abu Kuraib narrated: Muawiyah bin Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Sinan, on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Abu Jubayrah, on the authority of Zayd, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the Jews and said: Do you know why I sent to them? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: So I sent to them to ask them about the statement of God, ‘The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth.’ That on that day it will be white like silver. So when they came, he asked them, and they said: It will be white like black.”

c: Abu Ismail al-Tirmidhi told us: Abu Salih told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik,
m: that he recited this verse:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
. He said: God will replace it on the Day of Resurrection with an earth of silver on which no sins have been committed, and the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, will descend upon it.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: As if it were silver. Al-Hasan added in his hadith on the authority of Shababah: And the heavens are also like that, as if they were silver.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: An earth like silver, and the heavens are like that too.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Abu Hazim told me:
m: I heard Sahl ibn Saʿd say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure land like a pure loaf of bread. Sahl or someone else said: I have a teacher there for others.

x: Others said: It turns into fire.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated: Ibn Fadil narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr on the authority of Qais bin Al-Sakan who said: Abdullah said: The entire earth will be fire on the Day of Resurrection, and Paradise will be behind it, and you will see its cups and its full-breasted women. By the One in Whose Hand is Abdullah’s soul, a man will sweat profusely until his feet seep into the ground, then it will rise until it reaches his nose and he will not be called to account. They said: Why is that, O Abu Abd Al-Rahman? He said: Because of what people see and encounter.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Khathima, who said: Abdullah said:
m: The entire earth on the Day of Resurrection will be fire, and Paradise will be behind it, and you will see its maidens and its cups, and people will be bridled with sweat, or they will be overcome with sweat, but they will not reach the reckoning.

x: Others said: Rather, the earth will be replaced with a land of silver.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us:
m: I heard Al-Mughira Ibn Malik narrating on the authority of Al-Mujashiʿ or Al-Majashiʿi, Abu Musa was not sure, on the authority of someone who heard Ali say about this verse:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: The earth will be made of silver, and Paradise will be made of gold.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Malik, he said: A man from Banu Majashiʿ told me,
m: his name was Abdul Karim, or Ibn Abdul Karim, he said: This man told me, I think he was in Samarkand, that he heard Ali bin Abi Talib recite this verse,
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: The earth will be of silver, and Paradise will be of gold.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mughirah ibn Malik, on the authority of a man from Banu Majashi’,
m: whose name was Abd al-Karim, or whose nickname was Abu Abd al-Karim, who said: He appointed me to a man in Khurasan, and he said: This man told me that he heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
... the verse, so he claimed that it would be silver.

c: Muhammad bin Ismail told us: Abu Saleh told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan bin Saad, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said:
m: God will replace it on the Day of Resurrection with a land of silver.

x: Others said: He will exchange it for a loaf of bread.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saʿd Saʿid bin Dal from Saganian told us, he said: Al-Jarud bin Muʿadh Al-Tirmidhi told us, he said: Wakiʿ bin Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of ʿUmar bin Bishr Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: It will be replaced by white bread that the believer will eat from beneath his feet.

c: Al-Mini told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi,
m: or on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: On the Day the earth will be changed to another earth, he said: A loaf of bread from which the believers will eat from beneath their feet.

x: Others said: The land will be replaced by another land.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us: Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Kaʿb,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well], he said: The heavens will become gardens and the place of the sea will become fire. He said: And the earth will be replaced by another earth. Abu Kuraib narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will replace the earth with Surat Ibrahim 14:48 The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing. another earth, and the heavens with another earth. He will spread it out and level it, and extend it like the extension of a rough hide. You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness. Then God will warn the creation with a warning, and they will be in this replaced place in the same places as they were in the first. What was in its belly will be in its belly, and what was on its back will be on its back. That will be when He folds up the heavens like the folding of a scroll for a book, then He will roll them out. Then the earth will be replaced with another earth, and the heavens with another earth.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun Al-Awdi, who said:
m: The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white land, where no sin has been committed for forty years, and they will be bridled with sweat. Aisha said about that: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib, Hamid bin Mas’adah and Ibn Buzay’ told us:

c: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: I said: O Messenger of God, when the earth is replaced by another earth, and they emerge before God, the One, the Subduer, where will the people be on that Day? He said: On the Bridge.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah and Ibn Buzayʿ told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of ʿAmir, on the authority of ʿAishah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: “I said to Aisha: O Mother of the Believers, what do you think of the words of God, ‘
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well], and they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing.’ Where will the people be on that Day?” She said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: ‘On the Bridge.’”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Al-Hasan bin Anbasa Al-Warraq told us: Abd Al-Rahim told us,
m: meaning Ibn Sulayman Al-Razi, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the saying, On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth. I said: O Messenger of God, when the earth is replaced by another earth, where will the people be? He said: On the Bridge.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Asim bin Ali told us: Ismail bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Aisha,
m: the Mother of the Believers, who said: I was the first person to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse, and then he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us:
m: Rab’i bin Ibrahim Al-Asadi, the brother of Ismail bin Ibrahim, told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Amer, who said: “Aisha said: O Messenger of God, tell me, if the earth is replaced by another earth, where will the people be on that day? He said: On the bridge.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, he said: Al-Qasim told me, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan, he said: “Aisha said: O Messenger of God, ‘On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth,’ where will the people be on that Day? He said: No one has asked me about this thing. He said: On the bridge, O Aisha.”

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim told us: Al-Walid told me, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hassan ibn Bilal al-Muzani, on the authority of Aisha
m: that she asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God,
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well], he said: She said: O Messenger of God, where will the people be on that Day? He said: You have asked me about something that no one from my nation has asked me about, that is when the people will be on the bridge of Hell.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens as well, “It was mentioned to us that Aisha said: O Messenger of God, where will the people be on that Day? He said: You have asked about something that no one from my nation has asked me about before you. He said: They will be on the bridge of Hell on that Day.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “That Aisha asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to it, except that he said: On the path.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said:
m: “A Jewish rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Where will the people be on the Day when the earth is replaced by another earth? He said: They will be in the darkness beyond the Bridge.”

c: Muhammad bin Awn told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Saeed bin Thauban Al-Kila’i told us, on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, who said:
m: “A Jewish rabbi came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Do you see when God says in His Book, “
h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth

, and the heavens [as well],” then where will creation be at that time? He said: ‘They are the guests of God, and what He has will not fail them.’” The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: On the Day when the earth that we are on today will be replaced on the Day of Resurrection with another, and likewise the heavens today will be replaced with another, as He, the Most High, said. It is possible that what is replaced will be another earth of silver, and it is possible that it will be fire, and it is possible that it will be bread, and it is possible that it will be something else, and we do not have any report on this matter from the aspect that must be accepted as to which of them it will be, so no statement on this matter is correct except what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: and the heavens, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth
, he said: An earth like silver, and the heavens, likewise. And His statement:
h
And they will appear before God
, the One, the Prevailing, means:
h
And they will appear before God

, the One and Only in Lordship, Who subdues all things, and He overcomes them and directs them as He wills, however He wills. He brings His creation to life when He wills, and He causes them to die when He wills. Nothing can overcome Him, and nothing can overpower Him from their graves, alive for the Day of Resurrection.

evidence.text: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yahya bin Abbad told us: Hammad bin Zaid told us: Asim bin Bahdalah told us, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, that he recited this verse: On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing.

Abu Ismail al-Tirmidhi told us: Abu Salih told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that he recited this verse: On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth.

Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Malik, he said: A man from Banu Majashiʿ told me, his name was Abdul Karim, or Ibn Abdul Karim, he said: This man told me, I think he was in Samarkand, that he heard Ali bin Abi Talib recite this verse, On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, he said: The earth will be of silver, and Paradise will be of gold.

x: God Almighty says: And you will see the criminals, that Day, bound together in shackles.
God Almighty says: Their garments will be of pitch, and their faces will be covered by fire.

God Almighty says: And you will see those who disbelieved in God, and committed polytheism in this world, that Day, meaning: the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth and the heavens, bound together in shackles. He says: Their hands and feet bound to their necks with shackles, which are the bonds of a chain and a fetter, the singular of which is: safad, from which it is said: I bound him in the shackle, safadan and safadan, and safad is the fetter, and from it is the saying of Amr ibn Kulthum: They returned with the loot and the captives, and our sons with the kings in chains. Whoever makes one of these a chain, he pluralizes it as: chains, not chains. As for the gift, it is said from it: I chained him, chains, as Al-A’sha said: I hosted him one day, so he honored my company and made me a leader in the face of adversity. It was also said about giving: He handcuffed me, as Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani said: This is praise, if you listen to its speaker, then you will not be exposed to the curse of the shackles.
And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying, bound together in chains, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: bound in chains means: in bonds.

c: Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told me: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said:
m: The shackles are the chains.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Bound in chains, he said: Bound in shackles and chains.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ali bin Hashim bin Al-Barid told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-A’mash say: The chain.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: bound together in chains, he said: Their hands, feet, and necks were chained in it, and the chains are the shackles. His saying: Their garments are of pitch, meaning: their shirts that they wear, the singular of which is: sirbal, as Imru’ al-Qais said: Playful, you make me forget you if I dress you up Yunus told me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Their garments of pitch, he said: The garments are the shirts. And His statement: of pitch, he says: from the pitch that camels are comforted with, and there are three dialects for it: It is said: Qatran and Qatran with the opening of the qaf and the sukoon of the ta’ from it. And it was said: Isa bin Omar used to read from qatran with the breaking of the qaf and the sukoon of the ta’, and from it is the saying of Abu al-Najm: John looked like he was covered in tar and sackcloth from the sweat that dripped from his body. With the breaking of the qaf, and he also said: As if tar, when he recites it, the wind throws it to its path By breaking. And in a manner similar to what we said about that, whoever reads it will say the same.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: From tar meaning: the swaying camels’ udder.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: From tar. He said: The tar of camels.

x: Some of them said: Tar is copper.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Qatran means copper. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: From qatran means copper.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: From tar, he said: It is copper. And with this reading: I mean with the opening of the qaf and the kasra of the ta’, and making all of that one word, all the readers of the regions read that, and we read it with it because of the consensus of the proof from the readers on it. It has been narrated from some of the ancients that he used to read it from qatran with the qaf open, the ta’ silent, the ra’ tanween, and making an an from its description, and directing the meaning of qatr to mean copper, and the meaning of an, to mean that which has reached its peak in intensity. Among those who used to recite this, as we were told, was Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that.
m: He said: Al-Qasim told us. He said: Hisham told us. He said: Hisin told us on his authority. Those who interpreted this according to this reading mentioned the interpretation I mentioned in it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding his statement: Their garments will be of pitch, he said: pitch, and now: that which has reached its peak.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Dawud bin Mihran told us, on the authority of Yaqoub, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: that he used to recite: Their garments are of molten metal.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Affan told us: Al-Mubarak bin Fadala told us:
m: I heard Al-Hasan say: The Arabs used to say about something when its heat had reached its peak: This heat has come to an end. Hell has been kindled for it since it was created, so its heat has come to an end.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿid told us, he said: Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their garments will be of molten copper
. He said: The molten copper is copper, and now he says: Its heat has come, and that is because he says: scalding water has come.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Affan bin Muslim told us: Thabit bin Yazid told us: Hilal bin Khabab told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Their garments will be of molten copper
. He said: Of copper. He said: How can they be tormented with it?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: From a raindrop that has just come, he said: The raindrop that has just come is that which has reached its peak.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: From molten copper. He said: It is molten copper.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, from Qatar,
m: meaning: melted yellow.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Their garments are made of copper.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Hafs told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that he used to recite from Qatar that he said: From Safar, its heat has ended. Al-Hassan used to read it from tar. And His statement, And the Fire will cover their faces, means: And the Fire will scorch their faces and burn them, That God may recompense every soul for what it has earned, meaning: God did that to them as a recompense for what they earned of sins in this world, so that He may reward every soul for what it has earned of good and evil, so He will reward the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. Indeed, God is swift in account, meaning: God knows the deeds of every worker, so He does not need to count their deeds by counting them, nor by struggling, and He is swift in His account of their deeds. He has encompassed them with His knowledge, and nothing of them escapes Him, and He will recompense them for all of that, small and great.

evidence.text: With the breaking of the qaf, and he also said: As if tar, when he recites it, the wind throws it to its path By breaking.
And in a manner similar to what we said about that, whoever reads it will say the same.

And with this reading: I mean with the opening of the qaf and the kasra of the ta’, and making all of that one word, all the readers of the regions read that, and we read it with it because of the consensus of the proof from the readers on it.

It has been narrated from some of the ancients that he used to read it from qatran with the qaf open, the ta’ silent, the ra’ tanween, and making an an from its description, and directing the meaning of qatr to mean copper, and the meaning of an, to mean that which has reached its peak in intensity.
Among those who used to recite this, as we were told, was Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas.
Those who interpreted this according to this reading mentioned the interpretation I mentioned in it.
Al-Hassan used to read it from tar.

x: God Almighty says: This Qur’an is a message to the people, God conveyed it to them as an argument against them, and He excused them with what He revealed in it of His admonitions and lessons. And that they may warn thereby means: And that they may warn against the punishment of God, and beware of His vengeance. He revealed it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And that they may know that He is but One God means: And that they may know what He has used as evidence against them regarding what He has said about what is but One God, not various gods, as those who associate others with God say, and that there is no god but He, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, Who has subjected to them the sun and the moon, the night and the day, and sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for them, and has subjected to them the ships to sail in the sea by His command, and has subjected to them the rivers.

And that those of understanding may remember means: And that they may remember and be admonished by what God has used as evidence against him in the Qur’an, so that they may refrain from making a god other than Him, and associating anything with Him in worship. Other than him are the people of wisdom and reason, for they are the people of consideration and remembrance, unlike those who have no reason or understanding, for they are like livestock, rather they are more astray. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
This is a message for the people
, he said: the Qur’an. And that they may be warned thereby, he said: by the Qur’an. And that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may be reminded.

Aḥmad 5:122 (21166, Maymaniyya edition), Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:368—Abū al-Faḍl al-Zuhrī in his Ḥadīth (106), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān 8:44 transmitted it through various routes from Muḥammad ibn Abān. al-Nasāʾī transmitted it in al-Kubrā (11260) through various routes from Abū Isḥāq. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad transmitted it in Zawāʾid al-Musnad 5:122 (21167) through Muḥammad ibn Abān as a statement of a Companion. notes.en: Its source citation was given above, 7:619.

notes.ar: هو الأحوص الأنصارى، والبيت في ديوانه ص 153، وينسب أيضًا للمجنون وهو في ديوانه ص 200.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:72 to the author, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 72 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F write it without dots as “ḥibrasahu”; M reads “al-jabarūtiyya.” The author of al-Tāj emended the reading based on eighteen sources. See al-Tāj, root j-b-r.
notes.ar: رسمت في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف هكذا: "حبرسه" غير منقوطة، وفى م: "الجبروتية". وقد عدَّله صاحب التاج ثمانية عشر مصدرا. التاج (ج ب ر).

notes.en: Omitted in M, T1, and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: M reads: “against their enemies and opponents—that is, against those who oppose following the truth and avoiding its opposite.” See the two source citations.
notes.ar: في م: "على أعدائهم ومعانديهم، أي على من عاند عن اتباع الحق وتجنبه". وينظر مصدرى التخريج.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 410. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:73 to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 410، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 73 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: See al-Tibyān 6:282.
notes.ar: ينظر التبيان 6/ 282.

notes.en: M adds after it: “that is, one who turns away from following the path of truth.” al-Suyūṭī attributed the report in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:73 to the author.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "أي الحائد عن اتباع طريق الحق". والأثر عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 73 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ṣ and F read: “son.”
notes.ar: في ص، ف: "بن".

notes.en: M reads: “far.”
notes.ar: في م: "بعيد".

notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 341، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 73 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: الأهل وينظر تفسير القرطبي 9/ 350.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: M reads: “for a day when eyes stare fixedly.”
notes.ar: في م: "ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار".

notes.en: See al-Tibyān 6:282 and Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:403.
notes.ar: ينظر التبيان 6/ 282، وتفسير ابن كثير 4/ 403.

notes.en: This is Jarīr. The verse appears in his dīwān, p. 429.
notes.ar: هو جرير، والبيت في ديوانه ص 429.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "بذاك".

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 410; through its route al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (607).
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 410، ومن طريقه البيهقي في البعث والنشور (607).

notes.ar: بعده في م: "دمه و".

notes.en: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it in Ṣifat al-nār (87) through Saʿīd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (87) من طريق سعيد به.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr 1:341. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:74 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 341، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 74 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: M reads: “he can swallow it because of the severity of his thirst.”
notes.ar: في م: "يسيغه من شدة العطش".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “Bishr.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 19:13.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "بشر"، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 19/ 13.

notes.en: Ibn al-Mubārak transmitted it in al-Zuhd (314, Zawāʾid Nuʿaym); through him Aḥmad 5:265 (22339, Maymaniyya edition) and other sources transmitted it, including al-Zuhd, p. 20; al-Tirmidhī (2583); al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11263); Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ṣifat al-nār (73); al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (7460); al-Ḥākim 2:351; Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 8:182; al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (602); and al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr 4:342 and Sharḥ al-sunna (4405). al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:73 to Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: الزهد لابن المبارك (314 - زوائد نعيم)، ومن طريقه أحمد 5/ 265 (22339 - ميمنية)، وفي الزهد ص 20، والترمذى (2583)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11263)، وابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (73)، والطبراني في الكبير (7460)، والحاكم 2/ 351، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 8/ 182، والبيهقي في البعث (602)، والبغوى في تفسيره 4/ 342 وفي شرح السنة (4405)، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 73 إلى أبي يعلى وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:405—transmitted it through Baqiyya.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 405 - من طريق بقية به.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:74 to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 74 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 13:432 and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (611) transmitted it through Yazīd ibn Hārūn. Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ṣifat al-nār (126) and Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 4:212 transmitted it through al-ʿAwwām ibn Ḥawshab.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 432، والبيهقى في البعث والنشور (611) من طريق يزيد بن هارون به، وأخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (126) وأبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 212 من طريق العوام بن حوشب به.

notes.en: T1, T2, and F read: “it is said.”

notes.ar: هو عدي بن زيد العبادي، والبيت في معاني القرآن 732، وخزانة الأدب 5/ 191.

notes.en: This is Miskīn al-Dārimī; see his dīwān, p. 53. It is the second half of a verse whose opening is: “Our skins know the armor, and laugh…”
notes.ar: هو مسكين الدارمي ديوانه ص 53، وهذا عجز بيت صدره: * وتضحك عرفان الدروع جلودنا *

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F add after it: “if only.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "لو".

notes.en: This is Dhū al-Rumma; the verse appears in his dīwān 1:29. Sunna here means “form”; ghayr muqrifa means “not of mixed breed,” but of noble, pure stock; nadab means the scars left by wounds. See Abū Naṣr al-Bāhilī’s commentary on the dīwān, pp. 29–30.
notes.ar: هو ذو الرمة، والبيت في ديوانه 1/ 29. والسُّنَّة: الصورة، وقوله: غير مقرفة أي: ليست بهجينة، هي عتيقة كريمة، والنَّدَب: آثار الجراح. من شرح أبي نصر الباهلي للديوان ص 29، 30.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 74 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: M adds after it: “the wind upon it.”
notes.ar: بعده في م: "عليه الريح".

notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir recited khalaqa as a verb; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī recited khāliqa as a participle. See al-Sabʿa, p. 362; al-Taysīr, p. 109; and Ḥujjat al-qirāʾāt, p. 377.
notes.ar: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر: {خلق} على "فعل"، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (خالق) على "فاعل". السبعة ص 362 والتيسير ص 109، وحجة القراءات ص 377.

notes.en: T2 and F read: “followers.”
notes.ar: في ت 2، ف: "أتباع".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:74 to the author and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 74 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “by them.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "بهم".

notes.en: M reads: “a course of escape, by which they flee.” Ḥayṣ means fleeing and withdrawal; maḥīṣ means a turning aside, escape, or refuge; rāgha means to turn away from something. See Lisān al-ʿArab and Tāj al-ʿarūs, roots ḥ-y-ṣ and r-w-gh.
notes.ar: في م: "مزاغ يزوغون". والحَيص: الرَّواغ والتخلفُ. والمَحيص: المحيد والمعدل والمميل والمهرب. وراغ: مال وحاد عن الشيء. ينظر لسان العرب وتاج العروس (ح ي ص)، (ر و غ).

notes.en: M reads: “he turned away.”
notes.ar: في م: "زاغ".

notes.en: M, T1, T2, and F read: “ʿAmr.” His biography is in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr 6:190 and al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl 6:131.
notes.ar: في م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "عمرو". ترجمته في التاريخ الكبير 6/ 190، والجرح والتعديل 6/ 131.

notes.en: M reads: “he said, ‘then they gather.’”
notes.ar: في م: "قال فيجمعون".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and F read: “you endure”; M: “then they endured”; T2: “they endure.” The adopted reading is supported by the source citation.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "تصبروا"، وفى م: "فصبروا"، وفى ت 2: "يصبروا"، والمثبت من مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: Ṣifat al-nār reads: “a refuge.” Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted an extended, similar report in Ṣifat al-nār (251) through Ibn al-Mubārak.
notes.ar: في صفة النار: "ملجأ". والأثر أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (251) مطولًا بنحوه من طريق ابن المبارك به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T2, and F read: “and they said.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ف: "فقالوا".

notes.en: Ṣ and T2 read: “we beseech.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2: "نضرع".

notes.ar: ليس في: ت 1، والدر المنثور.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: M and al-Baghawī’s Tafsīr read: “then it wells up from”; Tārīkh Dimashq reads: “then it boils over.” The adopted reading agrees with the other sources.
notes.ar: في م، وتفسير البغوي: "فيثور من"، وفى تاريخ دمشق: "فيفور". والمثبت موافق لسائر المصادر.

notes.en: This is the wording in Ṣ, T2, F, al-Zuhd, and Sunan al-Dārimī. M and most sources read: “the disbelievers”; some have the equivalent wording “the unbelievers.”
notes.ar: كذا في: ص، ت 2، ف، والزهد وسنن الدارمي. وفى م وأغلب المصادر: "الكافرون". وجاء في بعضها بمعناه ولكن بلفظ "الكفار".

notes.en: M, al-Zuhd, and al-Baghawī’s Tafsīr read: “then his seat wells up.” Khalq afʿāl al-ʿibād and al-Durr al-manthūr read: “his seat wells up from”; Tārīkh Dimashq reads: “his seat boils over from.”
notes.ar: في م، والزهد، وتفسير البغوي: "فيثور من مجلسه". وفى خلق أفعال العباد، والدر المنثور: "فيثور مجلسه من". وفى تاريخ دمشق: "فيفور مجلسه من".

notes.en: M reads: “their wailing grows intense.”
notes.ar: في م: "يعظم نحيبهم".

notes.en: Ibn al-Mubārak’s al-Zuhd (Zawāʾid Nuʿaym, 374) has a similar report; through him al-Baghawī transmitted a similar version in his Tafsīr 4:345–346. al-Bukhārī in Khalq afʿāl al-ʿibād (469), al-Dārimī (2:327), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr 17:320–321, and Ibn ʿAsākir in Tārīkh Dimashq 7:453 transmitted a similar report through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād. al-Suyūṭī judged it weak in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:74–75 and attributed it to Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: الزهد لابن المبارك (زوائد نعيم: 374) نحوه، ومن طريق ابن المبارك أخرجه البغوي في تفسيره 4/ 345، 346 بنحوه. وأخرجه البخارى في خلق أفعال العباد (469)، والدارمي (2/ 327)، والطبراني في الكبير 17/ 320، 321، وابن عساكر في تاريخ دمشق 7/ 453 من طريق عبد الرحمن بن زياد به بنحوه. وضعفه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 74، 75 وعزاه لابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to the author, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Part of a longer report whose source citation was given above, p. 627, through Ibn al-Mubārak. The author quotes it here in separate portions; it appears at length in Ṣifat al-nār (251).
notes.ar: جزء من أثر طويل تقدم تخريجه في صفحة 627 من طريق ابن المبارك به، والمصنف يذكره هنا مفرقًا، وهو في صفة النار (251) مطولًا.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:341 through Maʿmar. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to Ibn al-Mundhir. In ʿAbd al-Razzāq and al-Suyūṭī, the wording is: “I cannot help you,” without the final half of the report.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 341 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى ابن المنذر، وعند عبد الرزاق والسيوطى بلفظ: " {ما أنا بمصرخكم} قال: ما أنا بمغيثكم" دون الشطر الأخير.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 لابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: M reads: “Iblīs, the truthful one.”
notes.ar: في م: "إبليس الصادق".

notes.en: M and F read: “ʿAmr”; the reading in T2 is unclear. See the preceding note on p. 627, n. 7.
notes.ar: في م، ف: "عمرو". وفى ت 2 غير واضحة. وينظر ما تقدم في صفحة 627 حاشية (7).

notes.en: Its source citation was given above, p. 627.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في صفحة 627.

notes.en: M reads: “their Lord permits them,” followed by “He says”; T1 and F read: “He says.” T2 is unclear.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to the author and Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.en: al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Duʿāʾ (1598), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt 1:272–273 (206), through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني في الدعاء (1598)، والبيهقى في الأسماء والصفات 1/ 272، 273 (206)، من طريق عبد الله بن صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: M reads: “in.”
notes.ar: في م: "في".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: al-Baghawī transmitted it in al-Jaʿdiyyāt 1:324 (111) through Shuʿba.
notes.ar: أخرجه البغوي في الجعديات 1/ 324 (111) من طريق شعبة به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F add after it: “like.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "مثل".

notes.en: M reads: “bunch.” Qanʿ and qināʿ can mean a tray made from palm fibers for holding food, or fruit; it is also said to be a tray for eating fruit and other foods. Ibn Barrī relates from Ibn Khālawayh that qināʿ specifically means a tray for fresh dates. Qinw is a cluster bearing its dates; ʿidhq is the stalk bearing its smaller clusters. See Lisān al-ʿArab, roots q-n-ʿ, q-n-w, and ʿ-dh-q.
notes.ar: في م: "بقنو". والقنع والقناع: الطَّبق من عُسب النخل يوضع فيه الطعام، وقيل: هو الذي يجعل فيه الفاكهة. وقيل: القنع؛ الطبق الذي تؤكل فيه الفاكهة وغيرها. وحكى ابن بري عن ابن خالويه: القناع طبق الرطب خاصة. والقنو: العذق بما فيه من الرُّطب. والعذق: العرجون بما فيه من الشماريخ. ينظر لسان العرب (ق ن ع)، (ق ن و)، (ع ز ق).

notes.en: al-Tirmidhī transmitted it 5:275–276 after report 3119 through Shuʿayb.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذى 5/ 275، 276 عقيب الحديث (3119) من طريق شعيب به.

notes.en: F reads: “al-Ḥanjāb”; al-Nasāʾī’s al-Sunan al-kubrā reads: “al-Ḥubāb.” He is Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Baṣrī, Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥabḥāb al-Azdī al-Maʿwalī. See his biography in Tahdhīb al-kamāl 12:509.
notes.ar: في ف: "الحنجاب"، وفى السنن الكبرى للنسائي: "الحباب". وهو أبو صالح البصرى شعيب بن الحبحاب الأزدى المعوليّ. ترجمته في تهذيب الكمال 12/ 509.

notes.en: al-Nasāʾī transmitted it in al-Kubrā (11262) through al-Naḍr.
notes.ar: أخرجه النَّسَائِي في الكبرى (11262) من طريق النضر به.

notes.en: al-Tirmidhī (3119), Abū Yaʿlā (4165), and Ibn Ḥibbān (475) transmitted a similar report through Ḥammād. al-Rāmahurmuzī transmitted a similar version in Amthāl al-ḥadīth, p. 72, through Shuʿayb.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذى (3119)، وأبو يعلى (4165)، وابن حبان (475) من طريق حماد به نحوه، وأخرجه الرامهرمزي في أمثال الحديث ص 72 من طريق شعيب به نحوه.

notes.en: M reads: “its root is firm”; F reads: “its root.”
notes.ar: في م: "أصلها ثابت"، وفى ف: "أصلها".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:76 to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Rāmahurmuzī in al-Amthāl.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76 إلى عبد الرزاق والترمذى وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والرامهرمزي في الأمثال.

notes.en: al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī transmitted a similar report in Mūḍiḥ awhām al-jamʿ wa-l-tafrīq 2:460–461 through al-Suddī.
notes.ar: أخرجه الخطيب البغدادى في موضح أوهام الجمع والتفريق 2/ 460، 461 من طريق السدى به نحوه.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author, with the addition “like a corrupt tree,” which he explained as colocynth.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف، بزيادة: {كشجرة خبيثة} قال: هي الحنظلة.

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: al-Rāmahurmuzī transmitted it in Amthāl al-ḥadīth, p. 72, through Abū Ḥudhayfa, with the wording: “The good tree is the date palm, and the corrupt tree is colocynth; this is the likeness of believer and unbeliever.”
notes.ar: أخرجه الرامهرمزى في أمثال الحديث ص 72 من طريق أبي حذيفة به، بلفظ: "الشجرة الطيبة النخلة، والخبيثة الحنظلة، مثل المؤمن والكافر".

notes.en: al-Rāmahurmuzī transmitted a similar extended report in Amthāl al-ḥadīth, pp. 71–72, through Ḥuṣayn.
notes.ar: أخرجه الرامهرمزى في أمثال الحديث ص 71، 72 من طريق حصين به نحوه، مطولًا.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “like.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "مثل".

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 عن معمرٍ به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “the date palms.” al-Suyūṭī attributed the report in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:76–77 to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr and al-Firyābī.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "النخل". والأثر عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76، 77 إلى سعيد بن منصور والفريابي.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Maʿmar, with the addition “and the corrupt tree is colocynth.”
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 عن معمر به، بزيادة "والشجرة الخبيثة الحنظلة".

notes.en: Jummār is the heart or core of a palm tree. See al-Nihāya 1:294.
notes.ar: الجُمَّار: هو جمع جُمَّارة. والجمارة: قلب النخلة وشحمتها. النهاية 1/ 294.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “the tree.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "الشجرة".

notes.en: al-Ḥumaydī in his Musnad 2:298 (676), Aḥmad 8:204–205 (4599), al-Bukhārī (72), and Muslim (64/2811) transmitted it through Sufyān.
notes.ar: أخرجه الحميدى في مسنده 2/ 298 (676)، وأحمد 8/ 204، 205 (4599)، والبخاري (72)، ومسلم (64/ 2811)، من طريق سفيان به.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:76 to the author and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76 إلى المصنف وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Imām Aḥmad transmitted it in 10:237–238 (6052) through ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, with the addition: “He said: ‘I mentioned this to ʿUmar, and he said, “My son, what kept you from speaking? By God, your saying that would have been dearer to me than such-and-such.”’” Aḥmad also transmitted it in 9:20 (5274) and 10:490–491 (6468); ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd (790), al-Bukhārī (61, 62, 131), Muslim (63/2811), and al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11261) transmitted it through various routes from Ibn Dīnār, some versions including the addition found in Aḥmad.
notes.ar: أخرجه الإمام أحمد 10/ 237، 238 (6052) من طريق عبد العزيز به، بزيادة: "قال: فذكرت ذلك لعمر، فقال: يا بنى، ما منعك أن تتكلم؟ فوالله لأن تكون قلت ذلك أحب إليَّ من أن يكون لي كذا وكذا". وأخرجه أيضًا الإمام أحمد 9/ 20 (5274)، 10/ 490، 491 (6468)، وعبد بن حميد (790) والبخارى (61، 62، 131)، ومسلم (63/ 2811)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11261) من طرق عن ابن دينار به، وفى بعض المواضع بزيادة مثل التي ذكرناها عند أحمد.

notes.en: Taḥāttu and related forms mean leaves falling from a branch or elsewhere. See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root ḥ-t-t.
notes.ar: يتحاتُّ: الحت والانحتات والتَّحات والتَّحتحُتُ: سقوط الورق عن الغصن وغيره. تاج العروس (ح ت ت).

notes.en: al-Bukhārī transmitted similar extended versions in report 6144 and al-Adab al-mufrad (360), with the wording “falling.” Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Marwazī in Taʿẓīm qadr al-ṣalāt (770), al-Rāmahurmuzī in al-Amthāl, p. 69, and Ibn Manda in al-Īmān (187) transmitted similar extended versions through Yaḥyā. al-Bukhārī (4698) and Muslim (64/2811) transmitted a similar extended version through ʿUbayd Allāh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى (6144)، وفي الأدب المفرد (360) - وجاء نحوه مطولًا فيهما، وبلفظ: "تحت" - ومحمد بن نصر المروزيُّ في تعظيم قدر الصلاة (770) نحوه مطولًا، والرامهرمزي في الأمثال ص 69 بنحوه، وابن منده في الإيمان (187) مطولًا، من طريق يحيى به. وأخرجه البخارى (4698)، ومسلم (64/ 2811) من طريق عبيد الله به نحوه مطولًا.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba, p. 47 (part one of volume four); Ibn Ḥazm in al-Muḥallā 8:430; and al-Bayhaqī 10:61 transmitted it through Abū Muʿāwiya.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة ص 47 (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع)، وابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 430، والبيهقي 10/ 61 من طريق أبي معاوية به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “Sulaymān.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "سليمان".

notes.en: al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted it in al-Mukhtāra 10:14 through ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:76–77 to al-Firyābī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الضياء في المختارة 10/ 14 من طريق على بن الجعد به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76، 77 إلى الفريابي وسعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75 to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. In 4:77 he attributed this wording to Ibn Abī Ḥātim: “every hour, night and day, winter and summer; this is the likeness of the believer, who obeys his Lord night and day, in winter and summer.”
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم. وعزاه 4/ 77 إلى ابن أبي حاتم بلفظ: "كل ساعة بالليل والنهار والشتاء والصيف، وذلك مثل المؤمن يطيع ربه بالليل والنهار والشتاء والصيف".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed an extended version in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:75–76 to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 75، 76 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم مطولًا.

notes.en: al-Baghawī mentions an extended version in his Tafsīr 4:347; Abū Ḥayyān also discusses it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ 5:422.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 4/ 347 مطولًا، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 5/ 422.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed an extended, similar report in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:76 to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 76 إلى المصنف بنحوه مطولًا.

notes.en: Ṣirām al-nakhl is the time when dates are ready to be harvested. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root ṣ-r-m.
notes.ar: صرام النَّخل، وصَرامه: أوان إدراكه. لسان العرب (ص ر م).

notes.en: Ibn Ḥazm transmitted it in al-Muḥallā 8:429 through Yaḥyā.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 429 من طريق يحيى به.

notes.en: Ibn Ḥazm transmitted a similar report in al-Muḥallā 8:430 through Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from ʿIkrima; it mentions ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, as will appear on p. 648. Its wording there is “We granted them enjoyment for a time” instead of “You will surely know its report…” and “He showed him the period from when it bears fruit until it is harvested…” al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar:
أخرجه ابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 430 من طريق هشام بن حسان عن عكرمة به نحوه، وفيه ذكر عمر بن عبد العزيز كما سيأتي في صفحة 648، وعنده {ومتعناهم إلى حين} بدل {ولتعلمن نبأه 
…. }، و "فأراه من حين تثمر إلى حين تصرم 
…. ". وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in al-Muṣannaf (11325) through Sufyān. Ibn Abī Shayba (part one of volume four), p. 47, transmitted it through two routes: Dāwūd, from ʿIkrima, and Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, from ʿIkrima. al-Bayhaqī 10:62 transmitted it through Ibrāhīm ibn al-Minhāl, from ʿIkrima.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في المصنف (11325) عن سفيان به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع) ص 47 من طريقى: داود عن عكرمة، وإبراهيم بن مهاجر عن عكرمة. وأخرجه البيهقي 10/ 62 من طريق إبراهيم بن المنهال، عن عكرمة.

notes.en: Ṣ, T2, and F read “taḥarrar,” without dots; M reads “taḥarruz.” Ḥazara means to cut something. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root j-z-r.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ف: "تحرر". غير منقوطة. وفى م: "تحرز". وحزر الشيءَ يجزُرُه ويجزِرُه جَزرًا: قطعه. اللسان (ج ز ر).

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributes the report in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author with this wording. He also attributes it there to the author, al-Firyābī, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim with the wording “it bears fruit every six months,” and to Ibn Abī Ḥātim with “the date harvest.”
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف بلفظه، وعزاه أيضا 4/ 77 إلى المصنف والفريابي وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم بلفظ: "تطعم في كل ستة أشهر"، وعزاه أيضا 4/ 77 إلى ابن أبي حاتم بلفظ: "جذاذ النخل".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba (part one of volume four), p. 47, transmitted it from Wakīʿ. It appears in Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 411, through ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd; al-Thawrī’s Tafsīr, p. 156, reads: “the period is a year.”
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع) ص 47 عن وكيع به، والأثر في تفسير مجاهد ص 411 من طريق عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد، وفي تفسير الثورى ص 156 بلفظ: "الحين السنة".

notes.en: al-Bayhaqī 10:62 transmitted a similar extended report through Saʿīd, with an addition at the beginning and the wording “every seven months.”
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي 10/ 62 من طريق سعيد به نحوه مطولًا - وفى أوله زيادة - بلفظ: "كل سبعة أشهر".

notes.en: Ibn Ḥazm transmitted it in al-Muḥallā 8:429 through Muḥammad ibn Thawr with the wording “between six and nine months”; ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 429 من طريق محمد بن ثور به بلفظ: "ما بين ستة أشهر إلى تسعة"، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 عن معمر به.

notes.en: A different route for this report was cited above, p. 646, n. 2, through Sufyān.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 646 حاشية (2) من طريق آخر عن سفيان به.

notes.en: M reads: “if.”
notes.ar: في م: "إن".

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and F read: “he cuts”; T2 reads: “cuts.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "يقطع"، وفى ت 2: "ـقطع".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba (part one of volume four), p. 47, transmitted it from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar. His version has “then he said” instead of “they both said.”
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع) ص 47 عن محمد بن جعفر به، وعنده: "فقال" بدل "قالا".

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 411, adds after it in Ṣ: “God willing, it is followed by: Yūnus related to me; he said, ‘Ibn Wahb informed us’; he said, ‘Ibn Zayd said concerning “it yields its fruit every season”: “every year.”’ May God bless our master Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace. In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. My Lord, make it easy. Abū Jaʿfar said…” T2 has similar material, except “My Lord, make it easy,” and adds “may God have mercy on him” at the end. T1 then adds “God knows best. Abū Jaʿfar said,” followed by a blank and unclear text; F adds “Abū Jaʿfar, may God have mercy on him.”
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 411، وبعده في ص: "يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى: حدثني يونس، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {تؤتي أكلها كل حين}. قال: كل سنة. وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله. وصحبه وسلم. بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، رب يسر، قال أبو جعفر"، ومثله في ت 2 عدا قوله: "رب يسر" وبزيادة "رحمه الله" في آخر الكلام. وبعده أيضا في ت 1: "والله أعلم. قال أبو جعفر" ثم بياض يتلوه كلام غير واضح. وبعده أيضا في ف: "قال أبو جعفر رحمه الله".

notes.en: al-Ṭūsī mentions it in al-Tibyān 6:291.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسي في التبيان 6/ 291.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba (part one of volume four), p. 47, and Saḥnūn in al-Mudawwana 2:117 transmitted it through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Salām. al-Shawkānī attributed it in Fatḥ al-qadīr 3:108 to Abū ʿUbayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع) ص 47، وسحنون في المدونة 2/ 117 من طريق أبي الأحوص سلامٍ به، وعزاه الشوكاني في فتح القدير 3/ 108 إلى أبي عبيد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T2, and F read: “ʿUsayl.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 17:154.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 2، ف: "عسيل". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 17/ 154.

notes.en: M and al-Durr al-manthūr read: “he knows.”
notes.ar: في م، والدر المنثور: "يعرف".

notes.en: al-Durr al-manthūr reads: “we know.”
notes.ar: في الدر المنثور: "ندرى".

notes.en: al-Bayhaqī 10:62 transmitted a brief version through Ibn al-Ghusayl. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي 10/ 62 من طريق ابن الغسيل به مختصرا، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba, p. 47 (part one of volume four), Ibn Ḥazm in al-Muḥallā 8:430, and al-Bayhaqī 10:62 transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Muslim. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة ص 47 (القسم الأول من الجزء الرابع)، وابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 430، والبيهقى 10/ 62 من طريق محمد بن مسلم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn Ḥazm transmitted it in al-Muḥallā 8:429 through Muḥammad ibn Thawr; ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Maʿmar. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن حزم في المحلى 8/ 429، من طريق محمد بن ثور به، وعبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Lisān al-ʿArab, root sh-r-y-n, says: “Sharīn is a hard tree from which bows are made; one tree is called sharīna.”
notes.ar: قال في اللسان: (شرين): هو شجر صُلب تتخذ منه القِسِيّ، واحدته شريانة.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to Ibn Mardawayh. See Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:413.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى ابن مردويه. وانظر تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 413.

notes.en: al-Baghawī transmitted it in al-Jaʿdiyyāt 1:537 (1142) through Shuʿba.
notes.ar: أخرجه البغوي في الجعديات 1/ 537، (1142) من طريق شعبة به.

notes.en: al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Tārīkh 4:216–217 through Ibn Jurayj. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخاري في تاريخه 4/ 216، 217، من طريق ابن جريج به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: al-Tirmidhī (3119) transmitted it through Ḥammād ibn Salama, from Shuʿba. al-Rāmahurmuzī in Amthāl al-ḥadīth, p. 72, transmitted it through Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Shuʿayb; ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Shuʿayb.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذى (3119) من طريق حماد بن سلمة عن شعبة به، والرامهرمزي في أمثال الحديث ص 72 من طريق حماد بن زيد عن شعيب به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 من طريق شعيب به.

notes.en: Ṣaffaqat al-rīḥ al-shayʾ means “the wind flipped something from side to side, turning it over.” See Lisān al-ʿArab, root ṣ-f-q.
notes.ar: صفَّقَت الريح الشيء: إذا قلبته يمينًا وشمالًا وردته. اللسان (ص ف ق).

notes.en: al-Rāmahurmuzī transmitted it in al-Amthāl, p. 72, through Abū Ḥudhayfa.
notes.ar: أخرجه الرامهرمزى في الأمثال ص 72 من طريق أبي حذيفة به.

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:77 to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 77 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذي (3119)، وابن حبان (475)، وأبو يعلى (4165) والحاكم (4165) من طرق عن حماد به.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 78 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “Saʿīd.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 10:290.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "سعيد"، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 10/ 290.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 3:377 and 13:367–368, al-Marwazī in Zawāʾid al-zuhd (1356), al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿa (867), and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (5) transmitted it through Abū Muʿāwiya. al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Awsaṭ (3664) through al-Aʿmash.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 3/ 377، 13/ 367، 368، والمروزى في زوائد الزهد (1356)، والآجرى في الشريعة (867)، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (5) من طريق أبى معاوية به، وأخرجه الطبراني في الأوسط (3664) من طريق الأعمش به.

notes.en: al-Ṭayālisī (781), al-Bukhārī (1369), Muslim (2871), al-Nasāʾī (2056), Ibn Mājah (4269), and others transmitted it through various routes from Shuʿba.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطيالسي (781)، والبخارى (1369)، ومسلم (2871)، والنسائي (2056)، وابن ماجه (4269) وغيرهم من طرق عن شعبة به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “Saʿīd.” See the source citations.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "سعيد". وينظر مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: al-Bukhārī (4699), Abū Dāwūd (4750), Ibn Manda in al-Īmān (1062), al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (3, 4), and al-Baghawī in Sharḥ al-sunna (1520) transmitted it through Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى (4699)، وأبو داود (4750)، وابن منده في الإيمان (1062)، والبيهقي في عذاب القبر (3، 4)، والبغوى في شرح السنة (1520) من طريق هشام بن عبد الملك به.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “al-Ḥasan.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 6:380.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "الحسن". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 6/ 380.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “tudrayt.” As for “wa-lā tulayt,” some say it means “nor did you recite or study,” from talā yatlū; they used yāʾ to match the yāʾ of darayt. Yūnus said it is instead wa-lā utlīt in Arabic, meaning that one’s camels had no offspring following them. Another view is “lā darayta wa-lā ittalyta,” from iftaʿala of alawtu, “I was able or capable.” Ibn al-Athīr says the correct form is wa-lā iʾtalayta. See al-Nihāya 14:195 and Lisān al-ʿArab, root t-l-w.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "تدريت". وقوله: "ولا تليت". قيل: معناه: ولا تلوت، أي لا قرأت ولا درست، من تلا يتلو، فقالوا: تليت. بالياء ليعاقب بها الياء في دريت، وقال يونس: إنما هو: ولا أتليت في كلام العرب معناه: أن لا تُتلى إبله، أي لا يكون لها أولاد تتلوها. وقال غيره: إنما هو: لا دريت ولا اتَّليت، على افتعلت من ألوت أي أطقت واستطعت. وقال ابن الأثير: والصواب، ولا ائتليت. ينظر النهاية 14/ 195، واللسان (ت ل و).

notes.en: al-Bazzār (872, Kashf) transmitted it from al-Ḥusayn and Muḥammad ibn Maʿmar al-Baḥrānī; Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunna (865) transmitted it from al-Ḥusayn; Aḥmad 17:32–34 (11000) transmitted it through Abū ʿĀmir al-ʿAqdī.
notes.ar: أخرجه البزار (872 - كشف) عن الحسين ومحمد بن معمر البحراني به، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (865) عن الحسين به، وأحمد 17/ 32 - 34 (11000) من طريق أبي عامر العقدى به.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in al-Muṣannaf (6324); Aḥmad 30:506 and 588 (18516, 18625), al-Ḥākim 1:38–39, al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (35), and al-Baghawī in Sharḥ al-sunna (1518) transmitted it through various routes from al-Aʿmash.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في المصنف (6324)، وأحمد 30/ 506، 588 (18516، 18625)، والحاكم 1/ 38، 39، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (35)، والبغوى في شرح السنة (1518) من طرق عن الأعمش به.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 3:310, 374, and 380; al-Marwazī in Zawāʾid al-zuhd (1219); Aḥmad 30:499 (18534); Abū Dāwūd (4753); and others transmitted it through Abū Muʿāwiya.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 3/ 310، 374، 380، والمروزى في زوائد الزهد (1219)، وأحمد 30/ 499 (18534)، وأبو داود (4753) وغيرهم من طريق أبي معاوية به.

notes.en: Abū Dāwūd (3212, 4753) and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (29) transmitted it through Jarīr.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو داود (3212، 4753)، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (29) من طريق جرير به.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 3:374 and 382, Aḥmad 30:506 (18535), Abū Dāwūd (4754), Ibn Manda (1064), al-Ḥākim 1:37, and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (33, 34) transmitted it through various routes from Ibn Numayr.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 3/ 374، 382، وأحمد 30/ 506 (18535)، وأبو داود (4754)، وابن منده (1064)، والحاكم 1/ 37، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (33، 34) من طرق عن ابن نمير به.

notes.en: al-Nasāʾī (2000) and Ibn Mājah (1549) transmitted it through ʿAmr ibn Qays.
notes.ar: أخرجه النَّسَائِي (2000)، وابن ماجه (1549) من طريق عمرو بن قيس به.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in al-Muṣannaf (6737); Aḥmad 30:576 (18614) and al-Ḥākim 1:39 transmitted it through Maʿmar. al-Ḥākim also transmitted it in 1:39 through Mahdī ibn Maymūn.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في المصنف (6737)، وأحمد 30/ 576 (18614)، والحاكم 1/ 39 من طريق معمر به، وأخرجه الحاكم أيضًا 1/ 39 من طريق مهدى بن ميمون به.

notes.en: al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (8) through Ādam. Aḥmad 14:234 (8563), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (2630), and al-Ḥākim 1:380–381 transmitted it through various routes from Ḥammād.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في عذاب القبر (8) من طريق آدم به، وأخرجه أحمد 14/ 234 (8563)، والطبراني في الأوسط (2630)، والحاكم 1/ 380، 381 من طرق عن حماد به.

notes.en: Ṣ and F read: “it took shape.”
notes.ar: في ص، ف: "تمثلت".

notes.en: M reads: “then he says.”
notes.ar: في م: "فيقول".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 3:383 transmitted it from Yazīd—meaning Ibn Hārūn—and ʿAbd al-Razzāq in al-Muṣannaf (6703) through Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 3/ 383 عن يزيد - هو ابن هارون - به، وعبد الرزاق في المصنف (6703) من طريق محمد بن عمرو به.

notes.en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunna (1429), al-Ṭabarānī (9145), and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (9) transmitted it through al-Masʿūdī.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (1429)، والطبراني (9145)، والبيهقي في عذاب القبر (9) من طريق المسعودى به.

notes.en: Muslim (74/2871), ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunna (1430), al-Nasāʾī (2055), Ibn Manda in al-Īmān (1063), and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (13) transmitted it through Sufyān.
notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (74/ 2871)، وعبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (1430)، والنسائي (2055)، وابن منده في الإيمان (1063)، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (13) من طريق سفيان به.

notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 30/ 435 (18482) عن عفان به، وقد تقدم تخريجه ص 658 حاشية (2)، ص 659 حاشية (1).

notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في عذاب القبر (256) من طريق محمد بن سعد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 79 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 3/ 330، 10/ 434 عن عباد به.

notes.en: al-Ṭayālisī (789), Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 9:56, and al-Bayhaqī in ʿAdhāb al-qabr (27) transmitted it through Abū ʿAwāna.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطيالسي (789)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 9/ 56، والبيهقى في عذاب القبر (27) من طريق أبي عوانة به.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 81 إلى المصنف.

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 عن معمر به.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 81 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr 1:342; al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Duʿāʾ (1626) through ʿAbd al-Razzāq. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:81 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 342، وأخرجه الطبراني في الدعاء (1626) من طريق عبد الرزاق به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 81 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 81 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and F read: “so you say”; T2 reads: “so he says.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "فتقول". وفي ت 2: "فيقول".

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “to him”; the adopted reading follows the two cited sources.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "إليه". والمثبت من مصدرى التخريج.

notes.en: Its source citation was given above, p. 665.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 665.

notes.en: M reads: “His blessings.”
notes.ar: في م: "نعمه".

notes.en: Ṣ, T2, and F read: “the king.” The verse appears in Ibn Hishām’s Sīra 2:419 and the author’s Tārīkh 3:64, attributed to Ibn al-Zibʿarā.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ف: "الملك". والبيت في سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 419، وتاريخ المصنف 3/ 64 منسوبا إلى ابن الزبعرى.

notes.en: Rāʾiq means “one who closes”; one says rataqtu al-shayʾ when one seals or closes something. See Sharḥ gharīb al-sīra 3:81.
notes.ar: الرائق: الساد، تقول: رتقت الشيء إذا سددته. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 81.

notes.en: al-Bukhārī transmitted a brief version in his Tārīkh 8:373 through Sufyān. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:84 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى في تاريخه 8/ 373 من طريق سفيان به مختصرا، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 84 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentions it in his Tafsīr 4:428 through Ḥamza al-Zayyāt. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:84 to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 428 عن حمزة الزيات به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 84 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: T1 and Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr, quoting Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s Tafsīr, read: “ibn Murra.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 22:302.
notes.ar: في ت 1، وتفسير ابن كثير نقلا عن تفسير ابن أبي حاتم: "بن مرة". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 22/ 302.

notes.en: Sufyān’s Tafsīr, p. 157; through its route al-Ḥākim transmitted it in 2:352 and said its chain is sound. Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:427—transmitted it through Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿUmar ibn Murra. Ibn Kathīr then says: “Abū Isḥāq also transmitted a similar report from ʿAmr Dhū Murra, from ʿAlī, and it is transmitted from him through other routes.” al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:84 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: تفسير سفيان ص 157، ومن طريقه الحاكم 2/ 352، وقال: صحيح الإسناد، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 427 - من طريق إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن عمر بن مرة، وقال ابن كثير عقبه: ورواه أبو إسحاق، عن عمرو ذي مر، عن علي نحوه، وروى من غير وجه عنه. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 84 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:427—transmitted it through Shuʿba. al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Dalāʾil 3:95 through Abū al-Ṭufayl, from ʿAlī. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:84 to Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 427 - من طريق شعبة به، وأخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل 3/ 95، من طريق أبي الطفيل، عن علي به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 84 إلى ابن الأنباري في المصاحف وابن مردويه.

notes.en: al-Nasāʾī transmitted it in al-Kubrā (11267) through Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted a different wording in his Tafsīr 1:342 through Abū al-Ṭufayl, from ʿAlī. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:85 to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Ḥākim in al-Kunā.
notes.ar: أخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11267) من طريق محمد بن جعفر به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 342 من طريق أبي الطفيل، عن علي بلفظ آخر. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 85 إلى ابن المنذر والحاكم في الكنى.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “ibn.” The emendation is correct; the Muslim mentioned is al-Baṭīn, cited in the preceding chain. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 27:526.

notes.en: The manuscripts read this way, but the correct form may be “depicted,” since Lisān al-ʿArab, root ṣ-n-m, says: “A ṣanam is something with a body or image; if it has neither, it is a wathan.”

notes.en: Lisān al-ʿArab’s version reads: “But when you face it, it is as though / a trunk for the eye, from Awāl, stripped bare.” Sarḥ describes a swift horse or camel. Awāl is a village, or a place near Syria. Mushadhdhab means a stripped trunk. See Lisān al-ʿArab, roots s-r-ḥ, ʾ-w-l, and sh-dh-b.
notes.ar:
رواية اللسان: أما إذا استقبلته فكأنه 
…. للعين جذع من أوال مشذب والسرح: يقال: خيل سرح وناقة سرح يعنى سريعة. وأوال: قرية، وقيل: اسم موضع مما يلى الشام. مشذب: جذع مشذب أي مقشر اللسان (س ر ح، أ و ل، ش ذ ب).

notes.en: The verse appears in Majāz al-Qurʾān 1:343, Lisān al-ʿArab, roots ṣ-w-m and q-d-m, and Asās al-balāgha, p. 1062. Rasal describes an easy-gaited camel. Jadīl is a twisted cord of leather or hair worn around a camel’s neck. Qaydūm means the front or foremost part of something; raʿn is a large mountain spur projecting forward; al-Ṣawwām is a mountain. See Lisān al-ʿArab, roots r-s-l, j-d-l, q-d-m, r-ʿ-n, and ṣ-w-m.
notes.ar: البيت في مجاز القرآن 1/ 343، واللسان (ص و م، ق د م)، وأساس البلاغة ص 1062. والرسل: يقال: جمل رسل: سهل السير. والجديل: حبل مفتول من أدم أو شعر يكون في عنق البعير أو الناقة. والقيدوم: قيدوم كل شيء: مقدمه وصدره والرعن: الأنف العظيم من الجبل تراه متقدما. والصوام: اسم جبل. اللسان (ر س ل، ج د ل، ق د م، ر ع ن، ص و م).

notes.en: ʿAḍāh refers to any large thorny tree. Ḥadaʾ is the plural of ḥadaʾa, a double-headed axe; waqīʿ means sharpened and pointed. The commentary likens her molars to sharp axes. Adapted from the dīwān’s note, p. 221.

notes.en: Sibawayh 1:177 and al-Kāmil 1:199 attribute the two verses to al-Shammākh. Al-Bakrī’s Arājīz al-ʿArab, p. 133, attributes the first verse, with other verses, to al-Jumayḥ, al-Shammākh’s nephew. Al-Shammākh’s dīwān, p. 389, attributes it to Jabbār ibn Juzaʾ. al-Tāj, root r-f-l, attributes it to Jandal ibn Ḥurrī, a scribal corruption of Jabbār ibn Juzaʾ. See the discussion of these variants in al-Khizāna 4:237.
notes.ar: البيتان نسبا للشماخ في سيبويه 1/ 177، والكامل 1/ 199. ونسب الأول منها مع أبيات أخر في أراجيز العرب للبكرى ص 133 للجميح بن أخى الشماخ، وفى ديوان الشماخ ص 389 نسب لجبار بن جزء، وفي التاج (رفل) نسب لجندل بن حرى، وهو تصحيف عن جبار بن جزء. وينظر الخلاف فيها في الخزانة 4/ 237.

notes.en: Ibn al-Athīr says: “One says nafadhanī baṣaruhu when his sight reaches and passes beyond me.” It is also said that the sight of the All-Merciful passes through all of them until it encompasses them; or that the observer’s sight passes over them because the plain is level. See al-Nihāya 5:91.
notes.ar: قال ابن الأثير: يقال: نفذنى بصره. إذا بلغنى وجاوزنى، وقيل: المراد به ينفذهم بصر الرحمن حتى يأتى عليهم كلهم. وقيل: أراد ينفذهم بصر الناظر؛ لاستواء الصعيد. النهاية 5/ 91.

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it in al-ʿIlal 2:176 (1215) from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar. al-Ḥākim 4:570 transmitted it through Shuʿba, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayra ibn Yarīm, from ʿAbd Allāh, and graded its chain sound. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:90 to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد في العلل 2/ 176 (1215) عن محمد بن جعفر به، وأخرجه الحاكم 4/ 570 من طريق شعبة عن أبي إسحاق عن هبيرة بن يريم عن عبد الله، وصحح إسناده. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 90 إلى عبد الرزاق وابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والبيهقي في البعث. =

notes.en: It was also transmitted as a prophetic report from ʿAbd Allāh: al-Bazzār (1859), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (10323) and al-Awsaṭ (7167), and Ibn ʿAdī 2:547 transmitted it. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:90 to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth. al-Bayhaqī said: “The version stopping at the Companion is more sound.”
notes.ar: = وقد روى عن عبد الله مرفوعا؛ أخرجه البزار (1859)، والطبراني في الكبير (10323)، وفى الأوسط (7167)، وابن عدى 2/ 547، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 90، إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه والبيهقي في البعث، وقال البيهقي: الموقوف أصح.

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الأهوال (69) عن علي بن الجعد به، وأخرجه أحمد 6/ 101 (الميمنية) من طريق القاسم به.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts. See the source citations and Tahdhīb al-kamāl 22:223.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted an extended version in his Muṣannaf (20884) through Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Thawbān. Muslim (315), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (9073), Ibn Khuzayma (232), Abū ʿAwāna 1:293, al-Ṭabarānī (1414), al-Ḥākim 3:481, Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 1:351, and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan 1:169 and Dalāʾil al-nubuwwa 6:263 transmitted an extended version through Abū Salām, from Abū Asmāʾ.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في مصنفه (20884) عن معمر عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن ثوبان مطولًا، وأخرجه مسلم (315)، والنسائى في الكبرى (9073)، وابن خزيمة (232)، وأبو عوانة 1/ 293، والطبراني (1414)، والحاكم 3/ 481، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 1/ 351، والبيهقي في سننه 1/ 169، وفي الدلائل 6/ 263 من طريق أبي سلام عن أبي أسماء به مطولًا.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “ʿAwn.” The adopted reading agrees with Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:438, quoting the author. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 26:236.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "عون". والمثبت موافق لما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 438 نقلًا عن المصنف، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 26/ 236.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 4:438—transmitted it through Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4:91 to Aḥmad and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil. See Fatḥ al-Bārī 11:375.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 438 - من طريق أبي بكر بن عبد الله بن أبي مريم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 91 إلى أحمد وأبي نعيم في الدلائل، وينظر فتح البارى 11/ 375.

notes.en: See above, p. 732.
notes.ar: تقدم في ص 732.

notes.ar: البيت في شرح القصائد السبع 412، وشرح القصائد التسع لابن النحاس 2/ 820.

notes.en: Here, the verb means that one coats camels with h ināʾ, tar, for mange. The form yahnaʾu is recited with three possible vowels on the nūn. See al-Tāj, root h-n-ʾ.
notes.ar: هنا الإبل يَهنَؤُها ويهنئها ويَهنُؤُها مثلثة النون؛ طلاها بالهِنَاءِ وهو القطران. التاج (هـ ن أ).
